title.zh: 卷六十五 列傳第十五: 高士廉 長孫無忌
title.en: Volume 65 Biographies 15: Gao Shilian, Zhangsun Wuji
title.raw: 卷六十五 列傳第十五: 高士廉 長孫無忌 Volume 65 Biographies 15: Gao Shilian, Zhangsun Wuji

sentences.zh: 高士廉 子履行 真行 長孫無忌

translations.literal: Gao Shilian; his sons Lüxing and Zhenxing; Zhangsun Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shilian; his sons Lüxing and Zhenxing; and Zhangsun Wuji.

sentences.zh: 高儉，字士廉，渤海蓚人。

translations.literal: Gao Jian, courtesy name Shilian, was a man of Su in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jian, styled Shilian, came from Su in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 曾祖飛雀，後魏贈太尉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Feique was posthumously made Grand Commandant by the Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Feique received a posthumous appointment as Grand Commandant from the Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖岳，北齊侍中、左僕射、太尉、清河王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yue served the Northern Qi as Palace Attendant, Left Vice Minister, Grand Commandant, and Prince of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yue had been Palace Attendant, Left Vice Minister, Grand Commandant, and Prince of Qinghe under the Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 父勵，字敬德，北齊樂安王、尚書左僕射、隋洮州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Li, courtesy name Jingde, was Prince of Le'an under the Northern Qi, Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs, and Governor of Taozhou under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li, styled Jingde, had held the titles of Prince of Le'an and Left Vice Minister under the Northern Qi and served as Governor of Taozhou under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 士廉少有器局，頗涉文史。

translations.literal: Shilian in his youth showed capacity and breadth of vision and had considerable acquaintance with literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shilian showed breadth of mind and had read widely in letters and history.

sentences.zh: 隋司隸大夫薛道衡、起居舍人崔祖浚並稱先達，與士廉結忘年之好，由是公卿藉甚。

translations.literal: Under the Sui, the Director of the Metropolitan Region Xue Daoheng and the Attendant Scribe Cui Zujun were both acclaimed as senior figures; they formed with Shilian friendships that ignored the difference in age, and thereby he became greatly esteemed among ministers and nobles.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Daoheng, Director of the Metropolitan Region, and Cui Zujun, Attendant Scribe—both regarded as senior men of letters under the Sui—became his friends across the gap in years, and from that time ministers and nobles spoke of him with high regard.

sentences.zh: 大業中，為治禮郎。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign period he served as a Gentleman for the Regulation of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era he held the post of Gentleman for the Regulation of Rites.

sentences.zh: 士廉妹先適隋右驍衛將軍長孫晟，生子無忌及女。

translations.literal: Shilian's younger sister had earlier been married to Zhangsun Sheng, General of the Right Valiant Cavalry under the Sui, and bore a son Wuji and a daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian's sister had earlier married Zhangsun Sheng, General of the Right Valiant Cavalry under the Sui, and bore a son, Wuji, and a daughter.

sentences.zh: 晟卒，士廉迎妹及甥於家，恩情甚重。

translations.literal: When Sheng died, Shilian welcomed his sister and nephew to his home and treated them with deep affection.
translations.idiomatic: After Sheng's death, Shilian took his sister and nephew into his household and cherished them with exceptional devotion.

sentences.zh: 見太宗潛龍時非常人，因以晟女妻焉，即文德皇后也。

translations.literal: Seeing that the future Taizong in his days as a hidden dragon was no ordinary man, he therefore gave him Sheng's daughter in marriage—she who became Empress Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Recognizing in the future Taizong, while he was still only a prince, a man out of the ordinary, he gave him Sheng's daughter in marriage—the future Empress Wende.

sentences.zh: 隋軍伐遼，時兵部尚書斛斯政亡奔高麗，士廉坐與交遊，謫為硃鳶主簿。

translations.literal: When the Sui army campaigned against Liaodong, the Minister of War Husizheng fled and defected to Goguryeo; Shilian was implicated for associating with him and was demoted to Registrar of Zhuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui campaign against Liaodong, Minister of War Husizheng fled to Goguryeo; because Shilian had been on friendly terms with him, he was banished to serve as Registrar of Zhuyuan.

sentences.zh: 事父母以孝聞，嶺南瘴癘，不可同行，留妻鮮于氏侍養，供給不足。

translations.literal: He was known for filial service to his parents; the miasma of Lingnan could not be braved together, so he left his wife Lady Xianyu to attend and support them, though provisions were insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned for filial devotion to his parents, he could not take them with him into the pestilential south of Lingnan; he left his wife, Lady Xianyu, to care for them, though means were scant.

sentences.zh: 又念妹無所庇，乃賣大宅，買小宅以處之，分其餘資，輕裝而去。

translations.literal: He also thought that his sister had no one to shelter her, so he sold the great house, bought a small house to lodge her in, divided the remaining funds, and departed with light baggage.
translations.idiomatic: Concerned that his sister had no refuge, he sold the family mansion, bought a smaller house for her, gave her what remained of the proceeds, and set out south with only light baggage.

sentences.zh: 尋屬天下大亂，王命阻絕，交趾太守丘和署為司法書佐。

translations.literal: Soon the realm fell into great disorder and imperial orders could not reach him; Qiu He, Administrator of Jiaozhi, appointed him Judicial Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the empire dissolved into chaos and imperial authority no longer reached the south; Qiu He, Administrator of Jiaozhi, appointed him Judicial Clerk.

sentences.zh: 士廉久在南方，不知母問，北顧彌切。

translations.literal: Shilian had long been in the south and had no word of his mother's condition; his longing as he looked north grew ever keener.
translations.idiomatic: Long stranded in the south with no news of his mother, he yearned toward the north with mounting anguish.

sentences.zh: 嘗晝寢，夢其母與之言，宛如膝下，既覺而涕泗橫集。

translations.literal: Once during a daytime nap he dreamed his mother speaking with him as though he were still at her knee; when he awoke, tears streamed down his face.
translations.idiomatic: Once he napped by day and dreamed his mother speaking to him as when he was a child at her knee; on waking, tears poured down his face.

sentences.zh: 明日果得母訊，議者以為孝感之應。

translations.literal: The next day he indeed received word from his mother; commentators took this as a response to filial feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The very next day news from his mother arrived; observers called it a sign of filial devotion answered from afar.

sentences.zh: 時欽州寧長真率眾攻和，和欲出門迎之，士廉進說曰：「長真兵勢雖多，懸軍遠至，內離外蹙，不能持久。

translations.literal: At that time Ning Changzhen of Qinzhou led his forces to attack Qiu He, and He wished to go out the gate to receive him; Shilian advanced and said: "Though Changzhen's troops are numerous, his army has come far from home; inwardly divided and outwardly pressed, it cannot last long.
translations.idiomatic: When Ning Changzhen of Qinzhou marched against him with an army, Qiu He meant to go out and submit; Shilian urged him: "Changzhen's host may look large, but it is an army far from home—riven within and harried without—and cannot hold out long.

sentences.zh: 且城中勝兵，足以當之，奈何而欲受人所制？

translations.literal: Moreover the city's crack troops are sufficient to meet them—why would you wish to place yourself under another's control?"
translations.idiomatic: The city's best troops are more than enough to meet them—why surrender yourself to another man's will?"

sentences.zh: 」和從之，因命士廉為行軍司馬，水陸俱進，逆擊破之，長真僅以身免，餘眾盡降。

translations.literal: " He followed this advice and therefore appointed Shilian Campaign Marshal; advancing by land and water together, they struck back and defeated the enemy; Changzhen barely escaped with his life, and the rest of the host surrendered entirely.
translations.idiomatic: He took the counsel, made Shilian Campaign Marshal, and advanced by land and water to rout the invaders; Changzhen fled with his life alone while the rest surrendered.

sentences.zh: 及蕭銑敗，高祖使徇嶺南。

translations.literal: When Xiao Xian was defeated, Gaozu sent forces to pacify Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Xian's defeat, Gaozu dispatched armies to bring Lingnan under control.

sentences.zh: 武德五年，士廉與和上表歸國，累遷雍州治中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wude, Shilian and Qiu He submitted a memorial to return to the realm and was repeatedly promoted to Assistant Administrator of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 5, Shilian and Qiu He memorialized their submission to the Tang court; he rose in due course to Assistant Administrator of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時太宗為雍州牧，以士廉是文德皇后之舅，素有才望，甚親敬之。

translations.literal: At that time the future Taizong was Governor of Yongzhou; because Shilian was the maternal uncle of Empress Wende and had long enjoyed reputation for talent, he treated him with great intimacy and respect.
translations.idiomatic: The future Taizong was then Governor of Yongzhou; knowing Shilian as Empress Wende's uncle and a man of long-standing talent and reputation, he drew him close and honored him.

sentences.zh: 及將誅隱太子，士廉與其甥長孫無忌並預密謀。

translations.literal: When the time came to execute the Hidden Crown Prince, Shilian and his nephew Zhangsun Wuji both took part in the secret planning.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot against the Hidden Crown Prince was set in motion, Shilian and his nephew Zhangsun Wuji both joined the secret council.

sentences.zh: 六月四日，士廉率吏卒釋繫囚，授以兵甲，馳至芳林門，備與太宗合勢。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the sixth month, Shilian led clerks and soldiers to release the bound prisoners, armed them, and galloped to the Fanglin Gate to be ready to join forces with Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the sixth month he led clerks and troops to free the prisoners, put arms in their hands, and raced to Fanglin Gate to unite with Taizong's force.

sentences.zh: 太宗升春宮，拜太子右庶子。

translations.literal: When Taizong entered the Eastern Palace, Shilian was appointed Right Vice President of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong became heir apparent, Shilian was named Right Vice President of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，擢拜侍中，封義興郡公，賜實封九百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was promoted and appointed Palace Attendant, enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing Commandery, and granted nine hundred households of substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 1 he was elevated to Palace Attendant, created Duke of Yixing, and granted a substantive fief of nine hundred households.

sentences.zh: 士廉明辯，善容止，凡有獻納，搢紳之士莫不屬目。

translations.literal: Shilian was clear in debate and graceful in bearing; whenever he offered remonstrance or counsel, the gentry all fixed their eyes upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Clear in argument and dignified in manner, he commanded the attention of the court whenever he spoke in counsel or remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 時黃門侍郎王珪有密表附士廉以聞，士廉寢而不言，坐是出為安州都督，轉益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: At that time the Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Wang Gui had a secret memorial which he entrusted to Shilian to present; Shilian kept it and did not speak of it, and for this was sent out as Military Governor of Anzhou and then transferred to Chief Administrator of the Great Area Command of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, once gave him a secret memorial to pass to the throne; Shilian suppressed it and said nothing, for which he was sent out as Military Governor of Anzhou and later made Chief Administrator of the Yizhou metropolitan command.

sentences.zh: 蜀土俗薄，畏鬼而惡疾，父母病有危殆者，多不親扶侍，杖頭掛食，遙以哺之。

translations.literal: The customs of Shu were shallow: people feared ghosts and loathed illness; when parents fell gravely ill, many would not attend them in person but hung food on a staff and fed them from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Shu folk were coarse in custom, fearing spirits and shunning the sick; when parents lay near death, many refused to nurse them at bedside, instead hanging food on a staff to feed them from a distance.

sentences.zh: 士廉隨方訓誘，風俗頓改。

translations.literal: Shilian instructed and guided them according to circumstance, and the customs changed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian instructed them as the case required, and local practice changed almost overnight.

sentences.zh: 秦時李冰守蜀，導引汶江，創浸灌之利，至今地居水側者，須直千金，富強之家，多相侵奪。

translations.literal: In Qin times Li Bing governed Shu, led the Min River, and created the benefit of irrigation; to this day land beside the water was worth a thousand gold, and powerful families often encroached upon one another.
translations.idiomatic: In Qin times Li Bing had governed Shu, diverted the Min River, and opened irrigation to the plain; land along the channels still fetched a fortune, and wealthy families constantly encroached on one another's water rights.

sentences.zh: 士廉乃於故渠外別更疏決，蜀中大獲其利。

translations.literal: Shilian then beyond the old channels opened new diversion works, and Shu gained great benefit thereby.
translations.idiomatic: He opened new channels beyond the old works, and Shu reaped a great increase in irrigated yield.

sentences.zh: 又因暇日汲引辭人，以為文會，兼命儒生講論經史，勉勵後進，蜀中學校粲然復興。

translations.literal: He also on leisure days gathered men of letters for literary gatherings, and at the same time ordered Confucian scholars to lecture on the classics and histories, encouraging the younger generation, so that schools in Shu brightly revived.
translations.idiomatic: In his spare hours he gathered literary men for salons, set scholars to lecture on the classics and histories, and encouraged the young; schools throughout Shu flourished again.

sentences.zh: 蜀人硃桃椎者，淡泊為事，隱居不仕，披裘帶索，沉浮人間。

translations.literal: Among the people of Shu was Zhu Taozhui, who took simplicity as his way, lived in seclusion without taking office, wore fur cloak and rope belt, and drifted through the world of men.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu there lived Zhu Taozhui, a man of austere simplicity who would not serve in office, clad in fur and rope, moving unnoticed through the world.

sentences.zh: 竇軌之鎮益州也，聞而召見，遺以衣服，逼為鄉正。

translations.literal: When Dou Gui governed Yizhou, he heard of him and summoned him, bestowed clothing upon him, and compelled him to become Village Head.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Gui governed Yizhou, he summoned Zhu, gave him clothes, and pressed him to accept the post of village head.

sentences.zh: 桃椎口竟無言，棄衣於地，逃入山中，結庵澗曲。

translations.literal: Taozhui in the end said not a word, cast the clothes upon the ground, fled into the mountains, and built a hut in a mountain dell.
translations.idiomatic: Taozhui never opened his mouth, threw the garments to the ground, fled into the hills, and built a hut beside a mountain stream.

sentences.zh: 夏則裸形，冬則樹皮自覆，人有贈遺，一無所受。

translations.literal: In summer he went naked; in winter he covered himself with tree bark; when people offered gifts, he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: In summer he went naked; in winter he wrapped himself in bark; he refused every gift offered him.

sentences.zh: 每為芒履，置之於路，人見之者，曰：「硃居士之履也」。

translations.literal: He would make straw sandals and place them on the road; those who saw them said, "These are the sandals of Master Zhu."
translations.idiomatic: He wove straw sandals and left them on the path; passersby would say, "Those are Master Zhu's sandals."

sentences.zh: 為鬻米置於本處，桃椎至夕而取之，終不與人相見。

translations.literal: He would set out rice for sale in its place; Taozhui came at evening to take it and in the end never met anyone face to face.
translations.idiomatic: He would leave rice for sale where he stood; Taozhui came at dusk to take payment and never let anyone see his face.

sentences.zh: 議者以為焦先之流。

translations.literal: Commentators regarded him as being of the same sort as Jiao Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Observers classed him with recluses such as Jiao Xian.

sentences.zh: 士廉下車，以禮致之，及至，降階與語，桃椎不答，直視而去。

translations.literal: When Shilian alighted from his carriage, he treated him with ceremony; when Taozhui arrived, Shilian descended the steps to speak with him, but Taozhui did not answer and went off staring straight ahead.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Shilian summoned him with full courtesy; when Zhu came, Shilian stepped down to speak with him, but Zhu made no reply and walked away without a glance aside.

sentences.zh: 士廉每令存問，桃椎見使者，輒入林自匿。

translations.literal: Shilian repeatedly sent people to inquire after his welfare; when Taozhui saw the messenger, he would enter the forest and hide himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian often sent messengers to inquire after him; at sight of them Zhu would slip into the woods and vanish.

sentences.zh: 近代以來，多輕隱逸，士廉獨加褒禮，蜀中以為美談。

translations.literal: In recent times many had slighted recluses, but Shilian alone honored them with praise and ceremony, and in Shu this became a celebrated tale.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times men of office had often scorned recluses, but Shilian alone treated Zhu with honor; the story became a favorite tale in Shu.

sentences.zh: 五年，入為吏部尚書，進封許國公，仍封一子為縣公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he entered the capital as Minister of the Civil Office, was advanced to Duke of Xu State, and at the same time enfeoffed one son as a county duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he returned to court as Minister of the Civil Office, was advanced to Duke of Xu, and enfeoffed one of his sons as a county duke.

sentences.zh: 獎鑑人倫，雅諳姓氏，凡所署用，莫不人地俱允。

translations.literal: He judged and appraised human conduct and was well versed in clan names; in every appointment he made, both the man and his background were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in judging character and deeply versed in pedigree, he made appointments in which both the man and his lineage won general assent.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，士廉攝司空，營山陵制度。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, Shilian acted as Minister of Works and planned the regulations for the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu's death, Shilian served as acting Minister of Works and oversaw the design of the imperial mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 事畢，加特進、上柱國。

translations.literal: When the task was finished, he was given the additional titles of Special Grand Master and Pillar of State of the Upper Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was done, he received the additional honors of Special Grand Master and Pillar of State of the Upper Rank.

sentences.zh: 是時，朝議以山東人士好自矜誇，雖復累葉陵遲，猶恃其舊地，女適他族，必多求聘財。

translations.literal: At that time court discussion held that the gentry of Shandong loved to boast themselves; though their houses had declined for many generations, they still relied on their old standing, and when a daughter married into another clan they invariably demanded heavy betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion held that Shandong families were prone to self-congratulation; though their lines had declined for generations, they still traded on old prestige and, when marrying daughters out, drove hard bargains for betrothal wealth.

sentences.zh: 太宗惡之，以為甚傷教義，乃詔士廉與御史大夫韋挺、中書侍郎岑文本、禮部侍郎令狐德棻等刊正姓氏。

translations.literal: Taizong detested this, holding that it gravely harmed moral teaching, and therefore ordered Shilian together with the Censor-in-Chief Wei Ting, the Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wende, the Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen, and others to revise and correct surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong abhorred the practice as a grave injury to public morals and ordered Shilian, Censor-in-Chief Wei Ting, Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wende, Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen, and others to compile a corrected register of clans.

sentences.zh: 於是普責天下譜諜，仍憑據史傳，考其真偽，忠賢者褒進，悖逆者貶黜，撰為《氏族志》。

translations.literal: Thereupon they broadly demanded genealogies from throughout the realm, still relying on historical records to examine truth and falsehood, advancing the loyal and worthy and demoting the perverse and rebellious, and compiled this as the Record of Clans.
translations.idiomatic: They then required genealogies from across the empire, checked them against historical sources, promoted loyal houses and demoted disloyal ones, and compiled the Record of Clans.

sentences.zh: 士廉乃類其等第以進。

translations.literal: Shilian then classified their ranks and grades and presented the work.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian arranged the clans by rank and presented the draft to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「我與山東崔、盧、李、鄭，舊既無嫌，為其世代衰微，全無冠蓋，猶自雲士大夫，婚姻之間，則多邀錢幣。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "I have had no old grievance with the Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng of Shandong, but because their generations have declined and they have no officials in caps and coaches, they still call themselves gentry; in marriage alliances they demand much money.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "I bear no old grudge against the Cui, Lu, Li, and Zheng of Shandong, but their houses have withered until none hold high office, yet they still style themselves gentry and squeeze bride-price from every marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 才識凡下，而偃仰自高，販鬻松檟，依託富貴。

translations.literal: Their talent and insight are mediocre, yet they hold their heads high; they peddle their ancestral graves and lean on the wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre in talent, they carry themselves as if above the world, trading on ancestral tombs and clinging to the rich.

sentences.zh: 我不解人間何為重之？

translations.literal: I do not understand why the world esteems them so.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot see why the world still honors them.

sentences.zh: 祗緣齊家惟據河北，梁、陳僻在江南，當時雖有人物，偏僻小國，不足可貴，至今猶以崔、盧、王、謝為重。

translations.literal: It is only because the Northern Qi held only Hebei, while Liang and Chen were remote in Jiangnan—though they had men of note at the time, they were petty states in outlying regions, not worth esteem—and to this day the Cui, Lu, Wang, and Xie are still held in honor.
translations.idiomatic: It is only because the Qi held the north while Liang and Chen were petty southern states—even when they had eminent men, their courts were too remote to count—and yet the world still ranks the Cui, Lu, Wang, and Xie above all.

sentences.zh: 我平定四海，天下一家。

translations.literal: I have pacified the four seas and made the realm one family.
translations.idiomatic: I have pacified the realm and made one family of the empire.

sentences.zh: 凡在朝士，皆功效顯著，或忠孝可稱，或學藝通博，所以擢用。

translations.literal: All who are in court have achieved conspicuous merit, or may be praised for loyalty and filial piety, or are broadly learned in arts and studies—that is why they were promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Every man at court was raised up for conspicuous service, for loyalty and filial devotion, or for breadth of learning—that is why he holds office.

sentences.zh: 見居三品以上，欲共衰代舊門為親，縱多輸錢帛，猶被偃仰。

translations.literal: Those now holding third rank and above who wish to ally by marriage with these declining old houses, even if they offer much money and silk, are still looked down upon.
translations.idiomatic: Men of third rank and above who seek marriage with these faded old houses may offer lavish gifts and still be treated with condescension.

sentences.zh: 我今特定族姓者，欲崇重今朝冠冕，何因崔干猶為第一等？

translations.literal: The reason I now specially fix clan names is that I wish to exalt the caps and coaches of the present court—why is the house of Cui Gan still placed in the first grade?
translations.idiomatic: I ordered this register to exalt the offices of the present day—why is the Cui clan of Gan still ranked first?

sentences.zh: 昔漢高祖止是山東一匹夫，以其平定天下，主尊臣貴。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Gaozu of Han was only a common man of Shandong, yet because he pacified the realm, the ruler was honored and the ministers were exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu of Han began as a common man of the east, yet by pacifying the realm he made ruler and minister alike illustrious.

sentences.zh: 卿等讀書，見其行跡，至今以為美談，心懷敬重。

translations.literal: When you read books you see his deeds, and to this day they are taken as a fine tale, and you harbor respect in your hearts.
translations.idiomatic: You read of his deeds in your books, still speak of them with admiration, and honor him in your hearts.

sentences.zh: 卿等不貴我官爵耶？

translations.literal: Do you not esteem my offices and ranks?
translations.idiomatic: Do you not hold my rank and titles in honor?

sentences.zh: 不須論數世以前，止取今日官爵高下作等級。

translations.literal: There is no need to discuss generations before this; take only the height or lowness of present offices and ranks to make the grades.
translations.idiomatic: Do not look back beyond the present—rank the clans solely by the offices they hold today.

sentences.zh: 」遂以崔干為第三等。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the house of Cui Gan was placed in the third grade.
translations.idiomatic: With that, the Cui of Gan was placed in the third rank.

sentences.zh: 及書成，凡一百卷，詔頒於天下。

translations.literal: When the book was completed it totaled one hundred juan, and an edict ordered it distributed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished—one hundred juan in all—an edict ordered it promulgated throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 賜士廉物千段，尋同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Shilian was granted a thousand bolts of goods, and soon served as co-equal with the Three Departments at the rank of third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian received a thousand bolts of silk as reward and soon held third-grade standing as a co-equal of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 十二年，與長孫無忌等以佐命功，並代襲刺史，授申國公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, together with Zhangsun Wuji and others for merit in assisting the founding mandate, they were all granted hereditary succession as regional inspectors, and he was created Duke of Shen State.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he and Zhangsun Wuji, among others, were rewarded for founding service with hereditary governorships, and Shilian was created Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 其年，拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: That same year he was appointed Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was appointed Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 士廉既任遇益隆，多所表奏，成輒焚稿，人莫知之。

translations.literal: As Shilian's appointment and favor grew ever higher, he submitted many memorials, but when they were finished he burned the drafts and no one knew their contents.
translations.idiomatic: As his standing rose, he submitted many memorials, yet burned each draft when done, so that none knew what he had written.

sentences.zh: 攝太子少師，特令掌選。

translations.literal: He acted as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and was specially ordered to direct selections.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and was specially charged with personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 十六年，加授開府儀同三司，尋表請致仕，聽解尚書右僕射，令以開府儀同三司依舊平章事。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was additionally granted the title of Honored Companion of the Palace with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies; soon he memorialized requesting retirement, was permitted to resign the Right Vice Ministry, and ordered to continue deliberating on affairs of state as Honored Companion with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he received the additional title Honored Companion of the Palace with Protocol of the Three Excellencies; he soon asked to retire, was released from the Right Vice Ministry, and continued to deliberate on state affairs in that capacity.

sentences.zh: 又正受詔與魏徵等集文學之士，撰《文思博要》一千二百卷，奏之，賜物千段。

translations.literal: He also received a formal edict together with Wei Zheng and others to gather men of letters and compile the Comprehensive Digest of Literary Thought in twelve hundred juan; when it was presented, he was granted a thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He was also formally ordered, with Wei Zheng and others, to gather scholars and compile the Comprehensive Digest of Literary Thought in twelve hundred juan; on its presentation he received a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月，詔圖形凌煙閣。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year an edict ordered his portrait painted in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventeenth year an edict ordered his portrait placed in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 十九年，太宗伐高麗，皇太子定州監國，士廉攝太子太傅，仍典朝政。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Taizong campaigned against Goguryeo; the Crown Prince supervised the realm from Dingzhou; Shilian acted as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent and still directed court governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, while Taizong campaigned against Goguryeo and the Crown Prince oversaw the realm from Dingzhou, Shilian served as acting Grand Tutor and continued to direct court affairs.

sentences.zh: 皇太子下令曰：「攝太傅、申國公士廉，朝望國華，儀刑攸屬，寡人忝膺監守，實資訓導。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince issued an order saying: "The acting Grand Tutor, Duke of Shen State Shilian, is the flower of the court's reputation and the model to which all look; I am unworthily charged with guardianship and truly rely on his instruction and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince issued an order: "Acting Grand Tutor, Duke of Shen Shilian, is the court's foremost exemplar; in my unworthy charge as regent I depend wholly on his guidance.

sentences.zh: 比聽政，常屈同榻，庶因諮白，少祛蒙滯。

translations.literal: When lately I attended to government, I often had him share my couch in deference, hoping that through consultation and explanation I might somewhat dispel my ignorance and obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: In recent audiences I have often had him share my couch so that, by question and answer, some of my ignorance might be cleared away.

sentences.zh: 但據案奉對，情所未安，已約束不許更進。

translations.literal: Yet he only answers me leaning on the desk, which my feelings cannot accept as proper; I have already restrained him and forbidden him to advance further.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he answers me only from across the desk, which I find unsatisfying, and I have already forbidden him to approach closer.

sentences.zh: 太傅誨諭深至，使遵常式，辭不獲免，輒復敬從。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor admonished me deeply and made me follow the usual forms; though I declined I could not be excused, and so I again respectfully obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor pressed me earnestly to keep to established form; unable to refuse, I obeyed once more.

sentences.zh: 所司亦宜別以一案供太傅。

translations.literal: The responsible offices should also separately provide a desk for the Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices should also set out a separate desk for the Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 」士廉固讓不敢當。

translations.literal: " Shilian firmly declined and dared not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian repeatedly declined, protesting that he was unworthy.

sentences.zh: 二十年，遇疾，太宗幸其第問之，因敘說生平，流涕歔欷而訣。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he fell ill; Taizong visited his residence to inquire after him and, as they recounted his life's course, wept and sighed in farewell.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he fell ill; Taizong came to his house, and as they spoke of his life together they wept and took their leave.

sentences.zh: 二十一年正月壬辰，薨於京師崇仁裡私第，時年七十二。

translations.literal: On the renchen day of the first month of the twenty-first year he died at his private residence in Chongren Lane in the capital; he was seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day of the first month of the twenty-first year he died at his home in Chongren Lane in the capital, aged seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 太宗又命駕將臨之，司空玄齡以上餌藥石，不宜臨喪，抗表切諫，上曰：「朕之此行，豈獨為君臣之禮，兼以故舊情深，姻戚義重，卿勿復言也。

translations.literal: Taizong again ordered his carriage to go in person; the Minister of Works Fang Xuanling, because the emperor was taking mineral medicines, held that he ought not attend the funeral and submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance; the emperor said: "This journey of mine is not only for the rites between ruler and minister, but also because the bond of old friendship is deep and the ties of marriage kin are weighty—do not speak of it again.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong prepared to go in person; Fang Xuanling, Minister of Works, argued that while the emperor was taking mineral drugs he must not attend a funeral and submitted a stern memorial; the emperor replied: "I go not only to fulfill the rites between ruler and minister, but because old friendship and marriage ties bind me to him—say no more."

sentences.zh: 」太宗從數百騎出興安門，至延喜門，長孫無忌馳至馬前諫曰：「餌石臨喪，經方明忌。

translations.literal: " Taizong followed by several hundred horsemen left by the Xing'an Gate; when he reached the Yanxi Gate, Zhangsun Wuji galloped to the front of his horse and remonstrated: "Taking mineral drugs while attending a funeral is clearly forbidden in the medical classics.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong rode out through Xing'an Gate with several hundred followers; at Yanxi Gate Zhangsun Wuji galloped up and pleaded: "Medical texts expressly forbid attending funerals while taking mineral drugs.

sentences.zh: 陛下含育黎元，須為宗社珍愛。

translations.literal: Your Majesty nourishes and cherishes the black-haired people and must treasure yourself for the sake of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty nurtures the people and must guard your person for the sake of the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣亡舅士廉知將不救，顧謂臣曰：『至尊覆戴恩隆，不遺簪履，亡歿之後，或致親臨。

translations.literal: My late uncle Shilian, knowing he would not be saved, turned to me and said: 'The August One's sheltering grace is profound and he has not cast off even my worn sandals; after my death he may come in person.
translations.idiomatic: My late uncle Shilian, knowing he would not recover, told me: 'The Son of Heaven has shown me boundless grace and has not cast me off even in my low estate; after my death he may come in person.

sentences.zh: 內省凡才，無益聖日，安可以死亡之餘，輒回宸駕，魂而有靈，負譴斯及。

translations.literal: Reflecting inward on my mediocre talent, I am of no benefit to the sage's days—how could I, in the remnant of death, turn back the imperial carriage? If my soul has awareness, the punishment would reach me.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of no talent and of no use to the throne—how could I, in death, draw the imperial carriage aside? If my spirit has consciousness, I would bear the guilt of that offense.'

sentences.zh: 』陛下恩深故舊，亦請察其丹誠。

translations.literal: ' Your Majesty's grace toward an old friend is deep; I also beg you to observe his sincere heart."
translations.idiomatic: Please weigh his sincere devotion to Your Majesty as an old friend."

sentences.zh: 」其言甚切，太宗猶不許。

translations.literal: " His words were very urgent, yet Taizong still would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: His plea was urgent, but Taizong still would not yield.

sentences.zh: 無忌乃伏於馬前流涕，帝乃還宮。

translations.literal: Wuji then prostrated himself before the horse weeping; the emperor thereupon returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji then prostrated himself before the horse in tears, and the emperor turned back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒、并州都督，陪葬昭陵，謚曰文獻。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Education and Military Governor of Bingzhou, buried with honor at Zhaoling, with the posthumous title Literary Offering.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Education and Military Governor of Bingzhou, interred at Zhaoling, and given the posthumous title Literary Offering.

sentences.zh: 士廉祖、父洎身，並為僕射，子為尚書，甥為太尉，當代榮之。

translations.literal: Shilian's grandfather, father, and he himself had all been Vice Ministers; his son was a Minister; his nephew was Grand Commandant—the age counted it glory.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather, father, and he himself had all served as vice ministers; his son became a minister; his nephew became Grand Commandant—the age regarded it as supreme honor.

sentences.zh: 六子：履行、至行、純行、真行、審行、慎行。

translations.literal: He had six sons: Lüxing, Zhixing, Chunxing, Zhenxing, Shenxing, and Shenxing.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Lüxing, Zhixing, Chunxing, Zhenxing, Shenxing, and Shenxing.

sentences.zh: 及喪柩出自橫橋，太宗登故城西北樓望而慟。

translations.literal: When the funeral bier came out from Heng Bridge, Taizong ascended the northwest tower of the old city wall and looked upon it in grief.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral procession crossed Heng Bridge, Taizong climbed the northwest tower of the old city wall and watched in anguish.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，追贈太尉，與房玄齡、屈突通並配享太宗廟庭。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, he was posthumously made Grand Commandant and, together with Fang Xuanling and Qutu Tong, granted joint sacrifice in Taizong's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong's accession he was posthumously made Grand Commandant and, with Fang Xuanling and Qutu Tong, granted a place in Taizong's ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 履行弟真行，官至右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Lüxing's younger brother Zhenxing reached the office of General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Lüxing's younger brother Zhenxing rose to General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 其子典膳丞岐，坐與章懷太子陰謀，事洩，詔付真行令自懲誡。

translations.literal: His son Qi, Director of Palace Provisions, was implicated in a secret plot with Crown Prince Zhanghuai; when the affair was exposed, an edict handed him to Zhenxing to punish and discipline himself.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi, Director of Palace Provisions, was implicated in Crown Prince Zhanghuai's conspiracy; when the plot was exposed, an edict entrusted him to Zhenxing to punish as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 真行遂手刃之，仍棄其屍於衢路。

translations.literal: Zhenxing thereupon killed him with his own hand and still cast his corpse upon the public road.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenxing then slew him with his own hand and cast the body into the street.

sentences.zh: 高宗聞而鄙之，貶真行為睦州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong heard of it and held it in contempt; he demoted Zhenxing to Prefect of Muzhou, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong heard of the affair, he was disgusted and demoted Zhenxing to prefect of Muzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌，字輔機，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji, courtesy name Fujii, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji, styled Fujii, was from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 其先出自後魏獻文帝第三兄。

translations.literal: His ancestors originated from the third elder brother of Emperor Xiaowen of the Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His line traced back to the third elder brother of Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 初為拓拔氏，宣力魏室，功最居多，世襲大人之號，後更跋氏，為宗室之長，改姓長孫氏。

translations.literal: Originally they were of the Tuoba clan, exerting strength for the Wei house; their merit was foremost, and for generations they inherited the title of Great Man; later they changed to the Ba clan, became chiefs of the imperial clan, and changed their surname to Zhangsun.
translations.idiomatic: They began as Tuoba clansmen who served the Wei with singular distinction, holding the hereditary title of Great Man for generations; later, as heads of the imperial clan under the Ba surname, they adopted the name Zhangsun.

sentences.zh: 七世祖道生，後魏司空、上黨靖王。

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor Daosheng was Minister of Works and Prince Jing of Shangdang under the Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations back, Daosheng had been Northern Wei's Minister of Works and Prince Jing of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 六世祖旃，後魏特進、上黨齊王。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Zhan was Special Advancement Grandee and Prince Qi of Shangdang under the Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations back, Zhan had been Special Advancement Grandee and Prince Qi of Shangdang under Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 五世祖觀，後魏司徒、上黨定王。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Guan was Minister over the Masses and Prince Ding of Shangdang under the Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations back, Guan had been Minister over the Masses and Prince Ding of Shangdang under Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 高祖稚，西魏太保、馮翊文宣王。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhi was Grand Tutor under Western Wei and Prince Wenxuan of Fenyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhi had been Grand Tutor under Western Wei and Prince Wenxuan of Fenyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖子裕，西魏衛尉卿、平原郡公。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Ziyu was Commandant of the Guards under Western Wei and Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Ziyu had been Commandant of the Guards under Western Wei and Duke of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖光，周開府儀同三司，襲平原公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guang was Honored Companion of the Palace with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies under Zhou and inherited the title Duke of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guang had been Honored Companion of the Palace with Protocol of the Three Excellencies under Northern Zhou and had inherited the dukedom of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 父晟，隋右驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: His father Sheng was General of the Right Valiant Cavalry under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng had been General of the Right Valiant Cavalry under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 無忌貴戚好學，該博文史，性通悟，有籌略。

translations.literal: Wuji was a noble kinsman who loved learning; he was broadly versed in literature and history, by nature penetrating and quick to understand, and possessed strategic planning.
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman of the imperial house, Wuji loved learning, was widely read in literature and history, quick of mind, and skilled in strategy.

sentences.zh: 文德皇后即其妹也。

translations.literal: Empress Wende was his younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wende was his younger sister.

sentences.zh: 少與太宗友善，義軍渡河，無忌至長春宮謁見，授渭北道行軍典簽。

translations.literal: In youth he was on friendly terms with Taizong; when the righteous army crossed the river, Wuji came to Changchun Palace to pay his respects and was appointed staff officer on the Weibei campaign circuit.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was close to the future Taizong; when Li Yuan's army crossed the Yellow River, Wuji came to Changchun Palace to pay homage and was made staff officer on the Weibei campaign.

sentences.zh: 常從太宗征討，累除比部郎中，封上黨縣公。

translations.literal: He often followed Taizong on campaigns; he was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Bureau of Review and enfeoffed as Duke of Shangdang County.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned repeatedly at Taizong's side, rose to Director in the Bureau of Review, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 武德九年，隱太子建成、齊王元吉謀，將害太宗，無忌請太宗先發誅之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Wude, the Hidden Crown Prince Jian Cheng and Prince of Qi Li Yuanji plotted and were about to harm Taizong; Wuji urged Taizong to strike first and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Wude, Crown Prince Jian and Prince of Qi Li Yuanji plotted to kill Taizong; Wuji urged him to strike first.

sentences.zh: 於是奉旨密召房玄齡、杜如晦等共為籌略。

translations.literal: Thereupon, by imperial order, he secretly summoned Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, and others to plan together.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's order he then secretly summoned Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, and others to lay plans.

sentences.zh: 六月四日，無忌與尉遲敬德、侯君集、張公謹、劉師立、公孫武達、獨孤彥雲、杜君綽、鄭仁泰、李孟嘗等九人，入玄武門討建成、元吉，平之。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the sixth month, Wuji together with nine others—Yuchi Jingde, Hou Junji, Zhang Gongjin, Liu Shili, Gongsun Wuda, Dugu Yanyun, Du Junchuo, Zheng Rentai, and Li Mengchang—entered the Xuanwu Gate to attack Jian Cheng and Yuanji and put down the revolt.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the sixth month, Wuji and nine companions—including Yuchi Jingde, Hou Junji, Zhang Gongjin, Liu Shili, Gongsun Wuda, Dugu Yanyun, Du Junchuo, Zheng Rentai, and Li Mengchang—entered the Xuanwu Gate, killed Jian Cheng and Yuanji, and ended the crisis.

sentences.zh: 太宗升春宮，授太子左庶子。

translations.literal: When Taizong was elevated to the Eastern Palace, Wuji was appointed Left Vice Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong became heir apparent, Wuji was appointed Left Vice Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 及即位，遷左武候大將軍。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Wuji was transferred to General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's accession, Wuji was made General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，轉吏部尚書，以功第一，進封齊國公，實封千三百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel; for merit ranked first he was advanced to Duke of Qi State with an enfeoffment of thirteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan he became Minister of Personnel; ranked first in merit, he was promoted to Duke of Qi with a fief of thirteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 太宗以無忌佐命元勳，地兼外戚，禮遇尤重，常令出入臥內。

translations.literal: Taizong, because Wuji was a founding merit minister and also an imperial kinsman by marriage, treated him with exceptional honor and often allowed him to enter and leave the inner sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wuji was both a founding minister and an imperial kinsman, Taizong honored him above others and often admitted him to the inner chambers.

sentences.zh: 其年，拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: That same year he was appointed Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was appointed Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時突厥頡利可汗新與中國和盟，政教紊亂，言事者多陳攻取之策。

translations.literal: At that time Jieli Khan of the Turks had newly made peace and alliance with China, but government and teaching were in disorder, and many who spoke on affairs urged strategies of attack and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jieli Khan of the Turks had just made peace with the Tang, yet his realm was in disorder, and many at court urged an attack.

sentences.zh: 太宗召蕭瑀及無忌問曰：「北番君臣昏亂，殺戮無辜。

translations.literal: Taizong summoned Xiao Yu and Wuji and asked: "The ruler and ministers of the northern tribes are muddled and chaotic, slaughtering the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong summoned Xiao Yu and Wuji and asked: "The northern tribes are in turmoil; their rulers slaughter the innocent.

sentences.zh: 國家不違舊好，便失攻昧之機；

translations.literal: If the state does not violate the old friendship, we lose the opportunity to attack when darkness prevails;
translations.idiomatic: If we honor the old alliance, we forfeit the chance to strike while they are weak;

sentences.zh: 今欲取亂侮亡，復爽同盟之義。

translations.literal: if we now wish to take advantage of chaos and insult the perishing, we again violate the righteousness of the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: yet if we seize on their disorder and strike the dying, we break the bond of alliance.

sentences.zh: 二途不決，孰為勝耶？

translations.literal: Between these two courses I cannot decide—which is superior?"
translations.idiomatic: I cannot choose between these two courses—which is the better path?"

sentences.zh: 」蕭瑀曰：「兼弱攻昧，擊之為善。

translations.literal: " Xiao Yu said: "To combine with the weak and attack the benighted—to strike is best.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu replied: "To join with the weak and strike the benighted—that is the better course.

sentences.zh: 」無忌曰：「今國家務在戢兵，待其寇邊，方可討擊。

translations.literal: " Wuji said: "At present the state is intent on sheathing arms; only when they raid the borders may we properly campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji said: "The state now seeks to keep the peace; we should strike only if they raid our borders.

sentences.zh: 彼既已弱，必不能來。

translations.literal: Since they are already weak, they surely cannot come.
translations.idiomatic: They are already too weak to mount a raid.

sentences.zh: 若深入虜廷，臣未見其可。

translations.literal: If we penetrate deep into the barbarian court, your subject does not see how that can succeed.
translations.idiomatic: A deep strike into their heartland, I do not see how that can succeed.

sentences.zh: 且按甲存信，臣以為宜。

translations.literal: Moreover, to keep the armor at rest and preserve good faith—your subject considers that fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold our armies in check and honor the alliance—that is my counsel.

sentences.zh: 」太宗從無忌之議。

translations.literal: " Taizong followed Wuji's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong accepted Wuji's advice.

sentences.zh: 突厥尋政衰而滅。

translations.literal: Before long the Turks' government declined and they perished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Turks' power collapsed and their khanate fell.

sentences.zh: 或有密表稱無忌權寵過盛，太宗以表示無忌曰：「朕與卿君臣之間，凡事無疑。

translations.literal: Someone submitted a secret memorial saying Wuji's power and favor were excessive; Taizong showed him the memorial and said: "Between you and me as ruler and minister, in all matters there is no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: When a secret memorial accused Wuji of excessive power and favor, Taizong showed it to him and said: "Between us as ruler and minister, there should be no hidden doubts.

sentences.zh: 若各懷所聞而不言，則君臣之意無以獲通。

translations.literal: If each harbors what he has heard and does not speak, then the intentions between ruler and minister cannot be brought into communication.
translations.idiomatic: If each of us keeps what he hears to himself, ruler and minister can never truly understand one another.

sentences.zh: 」因召百僚謂之曰：「朕今有子皆幼，無忌於朕，實有大功，今者委之，猶如子也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he summoned the hundred officials and said to them: "My sons are all still young; Wuji toward me has truly rendered great merit; in entrusting affairs to him now, it is as to a son.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned the officials and declared: "My sons are still young. Wuji has served me with great merit, and I entrust him now as I would a son.

sentences.zh: 疏間親，新間舊，謂之不順，朕所不取也。

translations.literal: To set the distant against the close, the new against the old—this is called disloyalty, and it is what I do not accept.
translations.idiomatic: To drive a wedge between close allies, to set newcomer against old companion—that I will not tolerate.

sentences.zh: 」無忌深以盈滿為誡，懇辭機密，文德皇后又為之陳請，太宗不獲已，乃拜開府儀同三司，解尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: " Wuji deeply took fullness and excess as a warning, earnestly declined confidential duties, and Empress Wende also pleaded on his behalf; Taizong, unable to do otherwise, then appointed him Honored Companion of the Palace with the Protocol of the Three Excellencies and released him from the Right Vice Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji took the warning to heart and begged to be relieved of confidential duties; Empress Wende pleaded for him as well. Unable to refuse, Taizong made him Honored Companion of the Palace with Protocol of the Three Excellencies and released him from the Right Vice Ministry.

sentences.zh: 是歲，太宗親祠南郊，及將還，命無忌與司空裴寂同升金輅。

translations.literal: That year Taizong personally sacrificed at the Southern Altar; when he was about to return, he ordered Wuji and Minister of Works Pei Ji to ascend the golden chariot together.
translations.idiomatic: That year, after Taizong performed the southern sacrifice, he ordered Wuji and Minister of Works Pei Ji to ride back with him in the imperial golden chariot.

sentences.zh: 五年，與房玄齡、杜如晦、尉遲敬德四人，以元勳各封一子為郡公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, together with Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, and Yuchi Jingde—the four of them—for founding merit each had one son enfeoffed as Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, and Yuchi Jingde were each granted a hereditary commandery dukedom for one son in recognition of founding merit.

sentences.zh: 七年十月，冊拜司空，無忌固辭，不許。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the seventh year he was formally invested as Minister of Works; Wuji firmly declined, but this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the seventh year he was invested as Minister of Works; Wuji protested firmly, but the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 又因高士廉奏曰：「臣幸居外戚，恐招聖主私親之誚，敢以死請。

translations.literal: He also memorialized through Gao Shilian, saying: "Your subject is fortunate to stand as an imperial kinsman by marriage and fears inviting the reproach that the sage ruler favors private kin; I dare beg with my life.
translations.idiomatic: He also pleaded through Gao Shilian: "As an imperial kinsman, I fear the charge that Your Majesty favors family over merit; I beg you with my life to refuse me.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「朕之授官，必擇才行。

translations.literal: " Taizong said: "When I confer office, I must select talent and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong replied: "When I grant office, I choose by talent and conduct alone.

sentences.zh: 若才行不至，縱朕至親，亦不虛授，襄邑王神符是也；

translations.literal: If talent and conduct do not measure up, even though one is my closest kin, I do not grant office without cause—Prince of Xiangyi Shen Fu is such a case;
translations.idiomatic: If a man lacks the talent and character for the post, even my closest kin receives nothing—Prince of Xiangyi Shen Fu is the example;

sentences.zh: 若才有所適，雖怨仇而不棄，魏徵等是也。

translations.literal: if talent is suited to the task, even though one is an enemy I do not cast him aside—Wei Zheng and others are such cases.
translations.idiomatic: but if a man's talent fits the need, I keep him even when he was once my enemy—Wei Zheng is the example.

sentences.zh: 朕若以無忌居後兄之愛，當多遺子女金帛，何須委以重官，蓋是取其才行耳。

translations.literal: If I were honoring Wuji only for the affection due an empress's elder brother, I ought to give his children much gold and silk—why need I entrust him with a weighty office? It is simply that I take his talent and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: If I favored Wuji only as my empress's brother, I would shower his children with gold and silk—why give him high office? I appoint him for his talent and character.

sentences.zh: 無忌聰明鑑悟，雅有武略，公等所知，朕故委之台鼎。

translations.literal: Wuji is bright, perceptive, and discerning, and elegantly possesses military strategy—you all know this; that is why I entrust him with the highest offices of state.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji is brilliant, discerning, and skilled in strategy—as you all know. That is why I place him at the summit of government.

sentences.zh: 」無忌又上表切讓，詔報之曰：「昔黃帝得力牧而為五帝先，夏禹得咎繇而為三王祖，齊桓得管仲而為五伯長。

translations.literal: " Wuji again submitted a memorial urgently declining; an edict answered him, saying: "Formerly the Yellow Emperor obtained Li Mu and became foremost among the Five Emperors; Yu of Xia obtained Gao Yao and became ancestor among the Three Dynasties; Duke Huan of Qi obtained Guan Zhong and became leader among the Five Hegemons.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji memorialized again, pleading urgently to decline. The emperor replied by edict: "The Yellow Emperor had Li Mu and led the Five Emperors; Yu of Xia had Gao Yao and stood first among the Three Dynasties; Duke Huan of Qi had Guan Zhong and headed the Five Hegemons.

sentences.zh: 朕自居籓邸，公為腹心，遂得廓清宇內，君臨天下。

translations.literal: Since I was in my princely residence, you have been my trusted inner counselor, and thereby I was able to clear the realm within the four seas and rule over all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: From my days as prince you have been my closest counselor, and through you I cleared the realm and came to rule the world.

sentences.zh: 以公功績才望，允稱具瞻，故授此官，無宜多讓也。

translations.literal: By your merit, achievement, talent, and public standing, you fully deserve the gaze of all; therefore I confer this office—there is no need for further refusal.
translations.idiomatic: Your merit, ability, and standing make you the man all look to; accept this office and decline no further.

sentences.zh: 」太宗追思王業艱難，佐命之力，又作《威鳳賦》以賜無忌。

translations.literal: " Taizong, recalling the hardships of establishing the royal enterprise and the strength lent by those who assisted the founding mandate, also composed the Rhapsody on the August Phoenix and bestowed it upon Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, remembering the hardships of founding the dynasty and the debt he owed his founding ministers, composed the Rhapsody on the August Phoenix and gave it to Wuji.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its words say:
translations.idiomatic: The poem reads:

sentences.zh: 有一威鳳，憩翮朝陽。

translations.literal: There was an august phoenix that folded its wings and rested facing the morning sun.
translations.idiomatic: There was an august phoenix, wings folded, resting in the light of the rising sun.

sentences.zh: 晨游紫霧，夕飲玄霜。

translations.literal: In the morning it wandered through purple mist; in the evening it drank dark frost.
translations.idiomatic: By morning it wandered through violet mist; by evening it drank the dark frost.

sentences.zh: 資長風以舉翰，戾天衢而遠翔。

translations.literal: Relying on the long wind to raise its pinions, it crossed the heavenly thoroughfare and soared far away.
translations.idiomatic: It rode the long wind to lift its wings and soared far along the roads of heaven.

sentences.zh: 西翥則煙氛閉色，東飛則日月騰光。

translations.literal: When it flew west, smoke and haze closed over all color; when it flew east, sun and moon flared with light.
translations.idiomatic: Flying west, it dimmed the very air; flying east, it made sun and moon blaze with light.

sentences.zh: 化垂鵬於北裔，馴群鳥於南荒。

translations.literal: Its transforming influence reached the great peng in the northern borderlands and tamed flocks of birds in the southern wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Its transforming power reached the great peng of the north and gentled whole flocks of birds in the southern wilds.

sentences.zh: 殄亂世而方降，應明時而自彰。

translations.literal: It extinguished a chaotic age and then descended; responding to a bright era, it revealed itself of its own accord.
translations.idiomatic: It came down only when chaos was ended, and in a bright age it showed itself without prompting.

sentences.zh: 俯翼雲路，歸功本樹。

translations.literal: It lowered its wings on the cloud-road and attributed its merit to the tree of its origin.
translations.idiomatic: It folded its wings along the cloud-road and gave the credit to the tree where it had nested.

sentences.zh: 仰喬枝而見猜，俯修條而抱蠹。

translations.literal: Looking up at the tall branches, it met with suspicion; looking down at the long boughs, it found them harboring borers.
translations.idiomatic: It looked up to the high branches and met suspicion; it looked down to the long boughs and found them riddled with worms.

sentences.zh: 同林之侶俱嫉，共干之儔並忤。

translations.literal: Companions of the same grove all envied it; fellows of the same trunk all took offense.
translations.idiomatic: Every bird of the same grove envied it; every creature of the same trunk turned against it.

sentences.zh: 無恆山之義情，有炎洲之凶度。

translations.literal: It had none of the righteous feeling of Mount Heng; it had the cruel measure of the Blazing Isles.
translations.idiomatic: They showed none of Mount Heng's steadfast loyalty, but all the savage temper of the southern isles.

sentences.zh: 若巢葦而居安，獨懷危而履懼。

translations.literal: Though others nested in reeds and dwelt at ease, it alone harbored peril and walked in fear.
translations.idiomatic: While others nested in reeds and lived at ease, it alone lived in dread, every step uncertain.

sentences.zh: 鴟鴞嘯乎側葉，燕雀喧乎下枝。

translations.literal: Owls and kites shrieked among the side leaves; swallows and sparrows clamored on the lower branches.
translations.idiomatic: Owls shrieked from the side leaves; swallows and sparrows clamored on the lower boughs.

sentences.zh: 慚己陋之至鄙，害他賢之獨奇。

translations.literal: Ashamed of their own ugliness to the utmost baseness, they harmed another's singular excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of their own ugliness, they sought to destroy one whose excellence stood alone.

sentences.zh: 或聚咮而交擊，乍分羅而見羈。

translations.literal: Sometimes they gathered beaks and struck together; sometimes they spread nets and caught it in restraint.
translations.idiomatic: At times they massed their beaks and attacked together; at times they spread their snares and held it fast.

sentences.zh: 戢凌雲之逸羽，韜偉世之清儀。

translations.literal: It folded its cloud-scaling soaring pinions and hid its pure bearing that awed the age.
translations.idiomatic: It folded the wings that had scaled the clouds and hid the noble bearing that had awed the world.

sentences.zh: 遂乃蓄情宵影，結志晨暉，霜殘綺翼，露點紅衣。

translations.literal: Thereupon it stored its feelings in the shadow of night and fixed its resolve in the light of dawn; frost marred its brocade wings, and dew spotted its crimson plumage.
translations.idiomatic: It nursed its grief through night's shadow and hardened its resolve at dawn; frost scarred its brocade wings, and dew spotted its crimson feathers.

sentences.zh: 嗟憂患之易結，嘆矰繳之難違。

translations.literal: It sighed that calamity and worry bind easily, and lamented that arrow and snare are hard to escape.
translations.idiomatic: It mourned how easily trouble takes hold, and how hard it is to evade the hunter's arrow and net.

sentences.zh: 期畢命於一死，本無情於再飛。

translations.literal: It expected to end its life in a single death and had no thought of flying again.
translations.idiomatic: It looked for death to end its ordeal and had no heart to take wing again.

sentences.zh: 幸賴君子，以依以恃，引此風雲，濯斯塵滓。

translations.literal: Fortunately it relied upon a gentleman, depending and trusting on him; he drew forth this wind and cloud and washed away that dust and filth.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately it found a noble man to lean on and trust; he summoned wind and cloud and washed away the stain.

sentences.zh: 披蒙翳於葉下，發光華於枝裡。

translations.literal: It parted the obscuring shade beneath the leaves and sent forth splendor within the branches.
translations.idiomatic: It cleared the gloom beneath the leaves and brought radiance back to the boughs.

sentences.zh: 仙翰屈而還舒，靈音摧而復起。

translations.literal: Its immortal pinions, bent, spread again; its numinous voice, broken, rose once more.
translations.idiomatic: Its sacred wings, once folded, spread wide again; its noble cry, once broken, sounded once more.

sentences.zh: 眄八極以遐翥，臨九天而高峙。

translations.literal: It gazed upon the eight extremities and soared into the distance; it faced the nine heavens and stood on high.
translations.idiomatic: It looked to the ends of the earth and soared afar; it faced the highest heaven and stood supreme.

sentences.zh: 庶廣德於眾禽，非崇利於一己。

translations.literal: It hoped to spread virtue among the many birds, not to exalt profit for itself alone.
translations.idiomatic: It sought to spread virtue among all birds, not to hoard glory for itself.

sentences.zh: 是以徘徊感德，顧慕懷賢。

translations.literal: Therefore it lingered, moved by virtue, and turned back in longing, cherishing the worthy man.
translations.idiomatic: So it lingered, grateful for his kindness, and turned back in admiration for the man who had saved it.

sentences.zh: 憑明哲而禍散，托英才而福全。

translations.literal: Relying on his bright wisdom, calamity dispersed; trusting in his outstanding talent, fortune was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: By his wisdom disaster was dispelled; in his protection its fortune was made whole.

sentences.zh: 答惠之情彌結，報功之志方宣。

translations.literal: The feeling of repaying kindness grew ever tighter; the resolve to requite merit was just then declared.
translations.idiomatic: Gratitude bound it ever closer; the will to repay his service now found its voice.

sentences.zh: 非知難而行易，思令後而終前。

translations.literal: It was not that it knew the hard and yet acted the easy; it thought to make what comes after continue what came before.
translations.idiomatic: Not because the easy path was chosen over the hard, but because it wished what came after to honor what had gone before.

sentences.zh: 俾賢德之流慶，畢萬葉而芳傳。

translations.literal: May the flowing celebration of worthy virtue be transmitted in fragrance through ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: May worthy virtue be celebrated and its fragrance handed down through ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 十一年，令與諸功臣世襲刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year an order was issued that he, together with the various merit ministers, should inherit the post of regional inspector in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he and the other founding ministers were granted hereditary regional governorships.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: The edict read:

sentences.zh: 周武定業，胙茅土於子弟；

translations.literal: King Wu of Zhou established the enterprise and enfeoffed with fiefs of thatch and earth his sons and younger kinsmen;
translations.idiomatic: King Wu of Zhou founded the dynasty and enfeoffed his sons and kinsmen with territorial fiefs;

sentences.zh: 漢高受命，誓帶礪於功臣。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han received the Mandate and swore that girdle and whetstone would be granted to his merit ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han received the Mandate and swore that his ministers would share girdle and whetstone forever.

sentences.zh: 豈止重親賢之地，崇其典禮，抑亦固磐石之基，寄以籓翰。

translations.literal: This was not merely to honor the lands of kin and the worthy and exalt their rites and ceremonies; it also fortified the foundation of bedrock and entrusted them with the role of frontier bulwark.
translations.idiomatic: This was not only to honor kin and the worthy and elevate their rites, but also to set bedrock under the throne and charge them with guarding the realm.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉已降，事不師古，建侯之制，有乖名實。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin downward, affairs no longer took antiquity as model; the system of establishing marquises departed from name and reality.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward, rulers ceased to follow the ancients, and the enfeoffment system lost touch with its name and purpose.

sentences.zh: 非所謂作屏王室，永固無窮者也。

translations.literal: This was not what is called making a screen for the royal house and securing it forever without end.
translations.idiomatic: This was no longer the true meaning of making a shield for the throne and securing the dynasty without end.

sentences.zh: 隋氏之季，四海沸騰，朕運屬殷憂，戡翦多難。

translations.literal: In the last days of the House of Sui the four seas seethed; my fate fell amid deep sorrow, and I cut down many calamities.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sui dynasty's final days the realm boiled in turmoil; fate placed me in grave peril, and I cut down one disaster after another.

sentences.zh: 上憑明靈之祐，下賴英賢之輔，廓清宇縣，嗣膺寶歷，豈予一人，獨能致此！

translations.literal: Above I relied on the aid of bright spirits; below I depended on the assistance of heroic worthies, and cleared the realm within the four seas and succeeded to the precious succession—how could I alone have brought this about!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's favor was above me and heroic ministers below; together we cleared the realm and I succeeded to the throne—surely I alone did not bring this about!

sentences.zh: 時迍共資其力，世安專享其利，乃睠於斯，甚所不取。

translations.literal: In times of hardship they together supplied their strength; in times of peace for the realm to enjoy the benefit alone—this is what I look back upon and greatly disapprove.
translations.idiomatic: They shared their strength in hardship; it would be wrong for me alone to enjoy the reward in peace—that I cannot accept.

sentences.zh: 但今刺史，即古之諸侯，雖立名不同，監統一也。

translations.literal: Yet the regional inspectors of today are the feudal lords of antiquity; though the names established differ, their oversight and governance are one.
translations.idiomatic: Today's prefects are the feudal lords of old; though the titles differ, their charge to govern is the same.

sentences.zh: 故申命有司，斟酌前代，宣條委共理之寄，象賢存世及之典。

translations.literal: Therefore I have charged the responsible offices to weigh the former ages, proclaim regulations and entrust the charge of joint governance, and preserve the precedent of enfeoffing the worthy with succession through generations.
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore ordered the responsible offices to consult past precedent, grant them governing authority, and preserve the ancient practice of passing merit from generation to generation.

sentences.zh: 司空、齊國公無忌等，並策名運始，功參締構，義貫休戚，效彰夷險，嘉庸懿績，簡於朕心，宜委以籓鎮，改錫土宇。

translations.literal: Minister of Works and Duke of Qi State Wuji and others all registered their names at the beginning of the Mandate; their merit joined in founding and construction, their righteousness ran through joy and sorrow, their efficacy shone in calm and peril, and their fine service and splendid achievements have been selected in my heart—they should be entrusted with frontier commands and have their lands and territories re-granted.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works and Duke of Qi Wuji and the others enrolled their names at the founding of the dynasty, shared in building the state, stood with me through hardship and ease, and proved their worth in peace and war—their splendid service has earned my trust. They shall be entrusted with frontier commands and granted new fiefs.

sentences.zh: 無忌可趙州刺史，改封趙國公；

translations.literal: Wuji is approved as Prefect of Zhao Prefecture and is re-enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao State;
translations.idiomatic: Wuji is appointed prefect of Zhao and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao;

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射、魏國公玄齡可宋州刺史，改封梁國公；

translations.literal: Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs and Duke of Wei State Xuanling is approved as Prefect of Song Prefecture and is re-enfeoffed as Duke of Liang State;
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Minister Fang Xuanling, Duke of Wei, is appointed prefect of Song and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Liang;

sentences.zh: 故司空、蔡國公杜如晦可贈密州刺史，改封萊國公；

translations.literal: The late Minister of Works and Duke of Cai State Du Ruhui is posthumously granted Prefect of Mi Prefecture and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Lai State;
translations.idiomatic: The late Minister of Works Du Ruhui, Duke of Cai, is posthumously granted the prefecture of Mi and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Lai;

sentences.zh: 特進、代國公靖可濮州刺史，改封衛國公；

translations.literal: Special Advancement Grandee and Duke of Dai State Jing is approved as Prefect of Pu Prefecture and is re-enfeoffed as Duke of Wei State;
translations.idiomatic: Special Advancement Grandee Li Jing, Duke of Dai, is appointed prefect of Pu and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Wei;

sentences.zh: 特進、吏部尚書、許國公士廉可申州刺史，改封申國公；

translations.literal: Special Advancement Grandee, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and Duke of Xu State Shilian is approved as Prefect of Shen Prefecture and is re-enfeoffed as Duke of Shen State;
translations.idiomatic: Special Advancement Grandee Gao Shilian, Minister of Personnel and Duke of Xu, is appointed prefect of Shen and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Shen;

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書、潞國公侯君集可陳州刺史，改封陳國公；

translations.literal: Minister of the Ministry of War and Duke of Lu State Hou Junji is approved as Prefect of Chen Prefecture and is re-enfeoffed as Duke of Chen State;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Hou Junji, Duke of Lu, is appointed prefect of Chen and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Chen;

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書、任城郡王道宗可鄂州刺史，改封江夏郡王；

translations.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Justice and Prince of Rencheng Commandery Daozong is approved as Prefect of E Prefecture and is re-enfeoffed as Prince of Jiangxia Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Li Daozong, Prince of Rencheng, is appointed prefect of E and re-enfeoffed as Prince of Jiangxia;

sentences.zh: 晉州刺史、趙郡王孝恭可觀州刺史，改封河間郡王；

translations.literal: Prefect of Jin Prefecture and Prince of Zhao Commandery Xiaogong is approved as Prefect of Guan Prefecture and is re-enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaogong, Prince of Zhao and prefect of Jin, is appointed prefect of Guan and re-enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian;

sentences.zh: 同州刺史、吳國公尉遲敬德可宣州刺史，改封鄂國公；

translations.literal: Prefect of Tong Prefecture and Duke of Wu State Yuchi Jingde is approved as Prefect of Xuan Prefecture and is re-enfeoffed as Duke of E State;
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jingde, Duke of Wu and prefect of Tong, is appointed prefect of Xuan and re-enfeoffed as Duke of E;

sentences.zh: 并州都督府長史、曹國公李勣可蘄州刺史，改封英國公；

translations.literal: Chief Secretary of the Bingzhou Area Command and Duke of Cao State Li Ji is approved as Prefect of Qi Prefecture and is re-enfeoffed as Duke of Ying State;
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji, Duke of Cao and chief secretary of the Bingzhou command, is appointed prefect of Qi and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Ying;

sentences.zh: 左驍衛大將軍、楚國公段志玄可金州刺史，改封褒國公；

translations.literal: General-in-Chief of the Left Xiaowei Guard and Duke of Chu State Duan Zhixuan is approved as Prefect of Jin Prefecture and is re-enfeoffed as Duke of Bao State;
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zhixuan, General-in-Chief of the Left Xiaowei Guard and Duke of Chu, is appointed prefect of Jin and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Bao;

sentences.zh: 左領軍大將軍、宿國公程知節可普州刺史，改封盧國公；

translations.literal: General-in-Chief of the Left Leading Army and Duke of Su State Cheng Zhijie is approved as Prefect of Pu Prefecture and is re-enfeoffed as Duke of Lu State;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zhijie, General-in-Chief of the Left Leading Army and Duke of Su, is appointed prefect of Pu and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Lu;

sentences.zh: 太僕卿、任國公劉弘基可朗州刺史，改封夔國公；

translations.literal: Minister of the Imperial Stud and Duke of Ren State Liu Hongji is approved as Prefect of Lang Prefecture and is re-enfeoffed as Duke of Kui State;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hongji, Minister of the Imperial Stud and Duke of Ren, is appointed prefect of Lang and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Kui;

sentences.zh: 相州都督府長史、鄅國公張亮可澧州刺史，改封鄖國公。

translations.literal: Chief Secretary of the Xiangzhou Area Command and Duke of Yu State Zhang Liang is approved as Prefect of Li Prefecture and is re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yun State.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang, Duke of Yu and chief secretary of the Xiangzhou command, is appointed prefect of Li and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yun.

sentences.zh: 余官食邑並如故，即令子孫奕葉承襲。

translations.literal: Their remaining offices and fief incomes shall all remain as before, and their descendants are immediately ordered to inherit in succession through generations.
translations.idiomatic: Their other offices and fief incomes shall remain unchanged, and their descendants shall inherit in succession from generation to generation.

sentences.zh: 無忌等上言曰：「臣等披荊棘以事陛下，今海內寧一，不願違離，而乃世牧外州，與遷徙何異。

translations.literal: Wuji and others submitted a memorial saying: "We Your ministers cleared thorns and brambles in serving Your Majesty; now within the seas there is peace and unity, and we do not wish to be separated from you—yet to hereditarily govern outer prefectures, how is this different from being banished?
translations.idiomatic: Wuji and the others submitted a memorial: "We endured hardship to serve Your Majesty. Now the realm is at peace, and we do not wish to leave you—yet to govern distant prefectures as hereditary fiefs, how is that different from exile?

sentences.zh: 」乃與房玄齡上表曰：

translations.literal: " Then together with Fang Xuanling they submitted a formal memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: " They then submitted a formal memorial together with Fang Xuanling:

sentences.zh: 臣等聞質文迭變，皇王之跡有殊；

translations.literal: We Your ministers have heard that substance and form change in turn, and the traces of emperors and kings differ;
translations.idiomatic: We have heard that forms of government change with the times, and that the ways of sage-kings differ across ages;

sentences.zh: 今古相沿，致理之方乃革。

translations.literal: Past and present follow one upon the other, and the methods of achieving good governance are therefore reformed.
translations.idiomatic: As custom passes from age to age, the methods of governing must also be revised.

sentences.zh: 緬惟三代，習俗靡常，爰制五等，隨時作教。

translations.literal: Looking back to the Three Dynasties, customs were inconstant; thereupon they instituted the five ranks, adapting instruction to the times.
translations.idiomatic: In the Three Dynasties, customs were unstable; the five feudal ranks were established and teaching adjusted to the times.

sentences.zh: 蓋由力不能制，因而利之，禮樂節文，多非己出。

translations.literal: This was because their strength could not control all, and so they turned it to advantage; rites, music, regulations, and forms mostly did not originate with the rulers themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Because they lacked the strength to rule directly, they turned necessity to advantage; much of the ritual and law did not come from the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 逮於兩漢，用矯前違，置守頒條，蠲除曩弊。

translations.literal: By the two Han dynasties, they corrected the earlier deviations, established regional governors and promulgated statutes, and abolished old abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Under the two Han dynasties, earlier errors were corrected; governors were appointed, regulations issued, and old abuses abolished.

sentences.zh: 為無益之文，覃及四方；

translations.literal: Though this created superfluous formalities, it spread throughout the four quarters;
translations.idiomatic: Though this bred needless formality, its benefits extended to all quarters of the realm;

sentences.zh: 建不易之理，有逾千載。

translations.literal: It established a governance that would not easily change, lasting more than a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: It established a durable order that endured for more than a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 今曲為臣等，復此奄荒，欲其優隆，錫之茅社，施於子孫，永貽長世。

translations.literal: Now, bending policy for us Your ministers, you revive this long-abandoned practice, wishing to honor and exalt us, grant us domains with altars of soil and grain, extend this to our descendants, and forever bequeath lasting glory.
translations.idiomatic: Now, for our sake alone, Your Majesty would revive this obsolete custom—honoring us with fiefs and altars of earth, granting them to our descendants for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 斯乃大鈞播物，毫髮並施其生；

translations.literal: This is like the great potter's wheel casting all things—every hair and tip alike receives life;
translations.idiomatic: This would be like the universal potter's wheel: the smallest creature receives life alike;

sentences.zh: 小人逾分，後世必嬰其禍。

translations.literal: Yet if petty men exceed their proper measure, later generations will surely suffer disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if lesser men overreach, later generations will surely suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: What is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 違時易務，曲樹私恩，謀及庶僚，義非僉允。

translations.literal: Going against the times and changing essential tasks, bending policy to plant private favor, taking counsel from ordinary officials—the principle is not one of unanimous approval.
translations.idiomatic: The times are wrong, the policy is misguided, favor is being dispensed privately, and ordinary officials were consulted—this is not a decision all can endorse.

sentences.zh: 方招史冊之誚，有紊聖代之綱。

translations.literal: It will soon invite reproach in the historical records and disorder the guiding principles of this sage age.
translations.idiomatic: It invites the reproach of history and disarranges the foundations of this enlightened age.

sentences.zh: 此其不可一也。

translations.literal: This is the first reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first reason it must not be done.

sentences.zh: 又臣等智效罕施，器識庸陋。
