translations.literal: Moreover, we Your ministers rarely put our wisdom to use, and our capacity and insight are mediocre and crude.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, we have rarely proved our worth, and our talent and judgment are mediocre.

sentences.zh: 或情緣右戚，遂陟台階；

translations.literal: Some rose to the steps of the hall through ties to imperial kin;
translations.idiomatic: Some of us rose through ties to the imperial kin;

sentences.zh: 或顧想披荊，便蒙夜拜。

translations.literal: Some, recalling how they cleared thorns for you, were honored with midnight appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Others were honored at midnight for clearing thorns in your service.

sentences.zh: 直當今日，猶愧非才，重裂山河，愈彰濫賞。

translations.literal: Even on this very day we still feel unworthy of our rank; to divide the mountains and rivers anew would only show how lavishly rewards have been dispensed.
translations.idiomatic: Even now we know ourselves unworthy; granting us new fiefs would only expose how lavish the rewards have been.

sentences.zh: 此其不可二也。

translations.literal: This is the second reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second reason it must not be done.

sentences.zh: 又且孩童嗣職，義乖師儉之方，任以褰帷，寧無傷錦之弊？

translations.literal: Moreover, if children succeed to office, this contradicts the principle of teaching thrift; to charge them with drawing aside the curtain of governance—will there not be the disaster of damaging the brocade?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if children inherit office, it violates the teaching of thrift; can we put them in charge of governance without ruining what they touch?

sentences.zh: 上干天憲，彝典既有常科，下擾生民，必致餘殃於後，一掛刑網，自取誅夷。

translations.literal: Above they would offend Heaven's ordinances; the eternal statutes already have fixed penalties; below they would disturb the people and surely bring lingering calamity upon later generations—once caught in the net of punishment, they would bring execution upon themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They would offend Heaven's law and the fixed penalties of statute; they would harm the people and bring disaster on their descendants—once entangled in the law, they would meet execution.

sentences.zh: 陛下深仁，務延其世，翻令剿絕，誠有可哀。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's deep benevolence seeks to extend their line, yet this would instead cut it off—a thing truly to be mourned.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's kindness aims to perpetuate their houses, yet this would destroy them—a thing truly pitiable.

sentences.zh: 此其不可三也。

translations.literal: This is the third reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third reason it must not be done.

sentences.zh: 當今聖歷欽明，求賢分政，古稱良守，寄在共理。

translations.literal: In the present sage reign, sagacity is honored, worthies are sought, and administration is shared; antiquity praised good prefects as those entrusted with joint governance.
translations.idiomatic: In this enlightened reign the wise are honored, talent is sought, and government is shared—as antiquity said, good prefects govern in partnership with the throne.

sentences.zh: 此道之目，為日滋久，因緣臣等，或有改張。

translations.literal: This principle has long been established; yet because of us Your ministers it might be changed.
translations.idiomatic: This principle has long stood; for our sake alone it might now be overturned.

sentences.zh: 封植兒曹，失於求瘼，百姓不幸，將焉用之？

translations.literal: To enfeoff and nurture our sons and nephews, neglecting to seek out suffering—if the people are unfortunate, what use are such men?
translations.idiomatic: To install our sons in office while neglecting the people's woes—if the people suffer, what good are such governors?

sentences.zh: 此其不可四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth reason it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth reason it must not be done.

sentences.zh: 在茲一舉，為損實多，曉夕深思，憂貫心髓。

translations.literal: In this one measure the actual harm is great; we ponder it morning and night, and worry pierces to the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: This single measure would do real harm; we ponder it day and night until worry pierces the marrow.

sentences.zh: 所以披丹上訴，指事明心，不敢浮辭，同於矯飾。

translations.literal: Therefore we lay bare our loyal hearts in this appeal, setting forth the facts to make our minds clear, not daring flowery words like those of pretended ornament.
translations.idiomatic: We speak plainly and lay our hearts bare, stating the facts without flowery pretense.

sentences.zh: 伏願天澤，諒其愚款，特停渙汗之旨，賜其性命之恩。

translations.literal: We humbly hope for Heaven's grace, that you will pardon our sincere foolishness, especially halt this broadly issuing edict, and grant us the kindness of sparing our lives.
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty to recognize our sincere folly, revoke this edict, and grant us the mercy of sparing our lives.

sentences.zh: 太宗覽表謂曰：「割地以封功臣，古今通義，意欲公之後嗣，翼朕子孫，長為籓翰，傳之永久。

translations.literal: Taizong read the memorial and said: "To grant land in enfeoffment to meritorious ministers is a principle common in past and present. I intended that your descendants should wing my posterity, long serve as frontier bulwarks, and pass this down forever.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong read the memorial and said: "Granting land to meritorious ministers is a principle honored in every age. I meant your descendants to support my own, serve as frontier bulwarks, and pass that charge down forever.

sentences.zh: 而公等薄山河之誓，發言怨望，朕亦安可強公以土宇耶？

translations.literal: Yet you slight the oath sworn over mountains and rivers and speak words of resentment and complaint—how could I force territory upon you?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you reject the oath sworn over mountains and rivers and speak with resentment—how could I force territory upon you?

sentences.zh: 」於是遂止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the matter was halted.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十二年，太宗幸其第，凡是親族，班賜有差。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Taizong visited his residence; all of his kin were granted gifts in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Taizong visited his home; all his relatives received gifts according to rank.

sentences.zh: 十六年，冊拜司徒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was invested and appointed Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was invested as Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 十七年，令圖畫無忌等二十四人於凌煙閣，詔曰：

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year an order was issued to have portraits painted of Wuji and twenty-three others in the Lingyan Pavilion; the edict said:
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he ordered portraits painted of Wuji and twenty-three others in the Lingyan Pavilion. The edict said:

sentences.zh: 自古皇王，褒崇勳德，既勒銘於鐘鼎，又圖形於丹青。

translations.literal: From antiquity emperors and kings have honored and exalted meritorious virtue, inscribing names upon bells and cauldrons and also depicting forms in red and green.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity emperors and kings have honored meritorious service, inscribing names on bells and cauldrons and painting portraits in red and green.

sentences.zh: 是以甘露良佐，麟閣著其美；

translations.literal: Therefore the worthy ministers of the Ganlu era had their excellence displayed in the Qilin Pavilion;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the worthy ministers of the Ganlu reign won fame in the Qilin Pavilion;

sentences.zh: 建武功臣，雲台紀其跡。

translations.literal: And the founding meritorious ministers had their traces recorded on the Cloud Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: And the founding ministers of Jianwu had their deeds recorded on the Cloud Terrace.

sentences.zh: 司徒、趙國公無忌，故司空、揚州都督、河間元王孝恭，故司空、萊國成公如晦，故司空、相州都督、太子太師、鄭國文貞公征，司空、梁國公玄齡，開府儀同三司、尚書右僕射、申國公士廉，開府儀同三司、鄂國公敬德，特進、衛國公靖，特進、宋國公瑀，故輔國大將軍、揚州都督、褒忠壯公志玄，輔國大將軍、夔國公弘基，故尚書左僕射、蔣忠公通，故陝東道行台右僕射、鄖節公開山，故荊州都督、譙襄公柴紹，故荊州都督、邳襄公順德，洛州都督、鄖國公張亮，光祿大夫、吏部尚書、陳國公侯君集，故左驍衛大將軍、郯襄公張公謹，左領軍大將軍、盧國公程知節，故禮部尚書、永興文懿公虞世南，故戶部尚書、渝襄公劉政會，光祿大夫、戶部尚書、莒國公唐儉，光祿大夫、兵部尚書、英國公勣，故徐州都督、胡壯公秦叔寶等，或材推棟樑，謀猷經遠，綢繆帷帳，經綸霸圖；

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses and Duke of Zhao Wuji; the late Minister of Works, Yangzhou Area Commander, and Prince Yuan of Hejian Xiaogong; the late Minister of Works and Duke Cheng of Lai Ruhui; the late Minister of Works, Xiangzhou Area Commander, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Duke Wenzhen of Zheng Zheng; Minister of Works and Duke of Liang Xuanling; Honorary Three Highest Offices with Staff Equal to the Three Distinguishers, Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Shen Shilian; the late General-in-Chief of the Left Xiaowei Guard and Duke Xiang of Tan Zhang Gongjin; General-in-Chief of the Left Leading Army and Duke of Lu Cheng Zhijie; the late Minister of the Ministry of Rites and Duke Wenyi of Yongxing Yu Shinan; translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Zhangsun Wuji, Duke of Zhao; the late Minister of Works Li Xiaogong, Yangzhou commander and Prince Yuan of Hejian; the late Minister of Works Du Ruhui, Duke Cheng of Lai; the late Minister of Works Wei Zheng, Xiangzhou commander, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Duke Wenzhen of Zheng; Minister of Works Fang Xuanling, Duke of Liang; Gao Shilian, Honorary Three Highest Offices, Right Vice Minister, and Duke of Shen; Yuchi Jingde, Honorary Three Highest Offices and Duke of E; Special Advancement Grandee Li Jing, Duke of Wei; Special Advancement Grandee Xiao Yu, Duke of Song; the late General Who Assists the State Duan Zhixuan, Yangzhou commander and Duke Zhongzhuang of Bao; General Who Assists the State Liu Hongji, Duke of Kui; the late Left Vice Minister Yin Tong, Duke Zhong of Jiang; the late Right Vice Minister of the Shandong Circuit Liu Kaishan, Duke of Yun; the late Jingzhou commander Chai Shao, Duke Xiang of Qiao; the late Jingzhou commander Qu Shunde, Duke Xiang of Pi; Luozhou commander Zhang Liang, Duke of Yun; Hou Junji, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Minister of Personnel, and Duke of Chen; the late General-in-Chief of the Left Xiaowei Guard Zhang Gongjin, Duke Xiang of Tan; General-in-Chief of the Left Leading Army Cheng Zhijie, Duke of Lu; the late Minister of Rites Yu Shinan, Duke Wenyi of Yongxing; the late Minister of Revenue Liu Zhenghui, Duke Xiang of Yu; Tang Jian, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Minister of Revenue, and Duke of Ju; Li Ji, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Minister of War, and Duke of Ying; the late Xuzhou commander Qin Shubao, Duke Zhuang of Hu, and others—some were pillars of state whose far-reaching counsel shaped strategy in the command tent;

sentences.zh: 或學綜經籍，德范光茂，隱犯同致，忠讜日聞；

translations.literal: Some mastered the classics, their moral example shone bright, they shared hardship and danger alike, and loyal remonstrance was heard daily;
translations.idiomatic: Some mastered the classics, shone as moral exemplars, shared hardship and peril, and offered loyal remonstrance day after day;

sentences.zh: 或竭力義旗，委質籓邸，一心表節，百戰標奇；

translations.literal: Some exerted their full strength under the banner of righteousness, pledged themselves at the princely residence, showed single-minded integrity, and marked extraordinary merit in a hundred battles;
translations.idiomatic: Some gave their all under the banner of righteousness, pledged themselves at the princely residence, served with single-minded loyalty, and won distinction in a hundred battles;

sentences.zh: 或受脤廟堂，闢土方面，重氛載廓，王略遐宣。

translations.literal: Some received the sacrificial meat in the court hall, opened territory on the frontiers, repeatedly cleared heavy miasmas, and spread the royal strategy afar.
translations.idiomatic: Some received the sacrificial oath in the court hall, opened territory on the frontiers, cleared repeated crises, and carried royal strategy to distant lands.

sentences.zh: 並契闊屯夷，劬勞師旅。

translations.literal: All shared hardship and peril, toiling in the hardship of campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: All shared hardship and peril, toiling through the campaigns.

sentences.zh: 贊景業於草昧，翼淳化於隆平。

translations.literal: They aided the founding enterprise in its dawn and winged pure transformation in a time of peace and prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: They helped build the dynasty in its dawn and supported its flourishing in a time of peace and prosperity.

sentences.zh: 茂績殊勳，冠冕列辟；

translations.literal: Outstanding achievements and exceptional merit crowned them among the feudal lords;
translations.idiomatic: Their splendid achievements crowned them among the feudal lords;

sentences.zh: 昌言直道，牢籠搢紳。

translations.literal: Their forthright counsel and upright ways won over the gentry officials.
translations.idiomatic: Their forthright counsel and upright conduct won over the gentry officials.

sentences.zh: 宜酌故實，弘茲令典，可併圖畫於凌煙閣。

translations.literal: It is fitting to consult former precedent and expand this excellent ordinance; their portraits may jointly be painted in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to consult precedent and expand this excellent ordinance; their portraits shall be painted together in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 庶念功之懷，無謝於前載；

translations.literal: Thus the thought of remembering merit may not fall short of former ages;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the intent to honor merit may not fall short of former ages;

sentences.zh: 旌賢之義，永貽於後昆。

translations.literal: The principle of honoring the worthy shall be forever bequeathed to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: The principle of honoring the worthy shall be bequeathed to generations yet to come.

sentences.zh: 其年，太子承乾得罪，太宗欲立晉王，而限以非次，回惑不決。

translations.literal: That year the Crown Prince Chengqian was found guilty of an offense; Taizong wished to establish the Prince of Jin, but was constrained because this violated the order of succession, and he wavered, unable to decide.
translations.idiomatic: That year Crown Prince Chengqian was disgraced. Taizong wished to establish the Prince of Jin, but because this violated the order of succession he wavered and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 御兩儀殿，群官盡出，獨留無忌及司空房玄齡、兵部尚書李勣，謂曰：「我三子一弟，所為如此，我心無憀。

translations.literal: He went to the Hall of the Two Ultimate Principles; all officials were dismissed and only Wuji, Minister of Works Fang Xuanling, and Minister of War Li Ji were kept behind. He said: "My three sons and one younger brother have acted as they have; my heart is restless.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the Hall of the Two Ultimate Principles, dismissed all officials, and kept only Wuji, Minister of Works Fang Xuanling, and Minister of War Li Ji. He said: "My three sons and one younger brother have behaved as they have; my heart is restless.

sentences.zh: 」因自投於床，抽佩刀欲自刺。

translations.literal: " Then he threw himself upon the bed, drew his girdle knife, and tried to stab himself.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he threw himself on the bed, drew his girdle knife, and tried to stab himself.

sentences.zh: 無忌等驚懼，爭前扶抱，取佩刀以授晉王。

translations.literal: Wuji and the others were shocked and afraid; they rushed forward to support and embrace him and took the knife from his girdle, handing it to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji and the others were terrified; they rushed forward to hold him and took the knife from his girdle, handing it to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 無忌等請太宗所欲，報曰：「我欲立晉王。

translations.literal: Wuji and the others asked what Taizong desired; he replied: "I wish to establish the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji and the others asked what Taizong wanted; he replied: "I wish to establish the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 」無忌曰：「謹奉詔。

translations.literal: " Wuji said: "We respectfully accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: " Wuji said: "We respectfully accept Your Majesty's command.

sentences.zh: 有異議者，臣請斬之。

translations.literal: Whoever voices disagreement, your minister asks to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever objects, your minister asks leave to behead him.

sentences.zh: 」太宗謂晉王曰：「汝舅許汝，宜拜謝。

translations.literal: " Taizong said to the Prince of Jin: "Your uncle has approved you; you should bow in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong said to the Prince of Jin: "Your uncle has approved you; bow in thanks.

sentences.zh: 」晉王因下拜。

translations.literal: " The Prince of Jin thereupon bowed.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince of Jin bowed.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂無忌等曰：「公等既符我意，未知物論何如？

translations.literal: Taizong said to Wuji and the others: "You have now accorded with my wish—what do you suppose public opinion will be?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said to Wuji and the others: "You have now agreed with my wish—what do you suppose public opinion will be?

sentences.zh: 」無忌曰：「晉王仁孝，天下屬心久矣。

translations.literal: " Wuji said: "The Prince of Jin is benevolent and filial; the realm has long looked to him.
translations.idiomatic: " Wuji said: "The Prince of Jin is benevolent and filial; the realm has long looked to him.

sentences.zh: 伏乞召問百僚，必無異辭。

translations.literal: I humbly beg that you summon and question the hundred officials—there will surely be no disagreement.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that you summon the hundred officials and ask them—there will surely be no dissent.

sentences.zh: 若不蹈舞同音，臣負陛下萬死。

translations.literal: If they do not leap and dance with one voice, your minister deserves ten thousand deaths before Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: If they do not leap and shout as one, your minister deserves ten thousand deaths.

sentences.zh: 」於是建立遂定，因加授無忌太子太師。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the establishment of the heir was settled, and Wuji was additionally appointed Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the succession was settled, and Wuji was additionally appointed Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋而太宗又欲立吳王恪，無忌密爭之，其事遂輟。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Taizong again wished to establish Prince of Wu Ke; Wuji privately remonstrated against it, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Taizong again wished to establish Prince of Wu Li Ke; Wuji privately remonstrated, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗謂無忌等曰：「朕聞主賢則臣直，人苦不自知，公宜面論，攻朕得失。

translations.literal: Taizong once said to Wuji and the others: "I have heard that when the ruler is worthy, ministers are upright; people find it hard to know themselves. You should speak frankly before me and assail my strengths and faults.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once said to Wuji and the others: "I have heard that when the ruler is worthy, ministers are upright, but people find it hard to know themselves. Speak frankly before me and criticize my strengths and faults.

sentences.zh: 」無忌奏言：「陛下武功文德，跨絕古今，發號施令，事皆利物。

translations.literal: " Wuji submitted: "Your Majesty's martial achievements and civil virtue surpass all past and present; when you issue commands and orders, every measure benefits the people.
translations.idiomatic: " Wuji submitted: "Your Majesty's martial achievements and civil virtue surpass all past and present; every command you issue benefits the people.

sentences.zh: 《孝經》云：『將順其美。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: 'Develop and follow what is good in him.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety says: 'Develop and follow what is good in him.

sentences.zh: 』臣順之不暇，實不見陛下有所愆失。

translations.literal: ' Your minister has no leisure even to follow along—I truly see no fault or failing in Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: ' Your minister has no leisure even to follow along—I truly see no fault in Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「朕冀聞己過，公乃妄相諛悅。

translations.literal: " Taizong said: "I hoped to hear of my faults, yet you falsely flatter and please me.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong said: "I hoped to hear of my faults, yet you falsely flatter me.

sentences.zh: 朕今面談公等得失，以為鑑誡。

translations.literal: I will now speak face to face of your strengths and faults as a warning and lesson.
translations.idiomatic: I will now speak frankly of your strengths and faults as a warning and lesson.

sentences.zh: 言之者可以無過，聞之者可以自改。

translations.literal: Those who speak may be without fault; those who hear may reform themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Those who speak may be without fault; those who hear may reform themselves.

sentences.zh: 」因目無忌曰：「善避嫌疑，應對敏速，求之古人，亦當無比；

translations.literal: " He then looked at Wuji and said: "You are skilled at avoiding suspicion, quick and agile in response—sought among the ancients, you would likewise have no equal;
translations.idiomatic: " He then looked at Wuji and said: "You are skilled at avoiding suspicion and quick in response—sought among the ancients, you would have no equal;

sentences.zh: 而總兵攻戰，非所長也。

translations.literal: Yet commanding troops in attack and battle is not your strong point.
translations.idiomatic: Yet commanding troops in attack and battle is not your strong point.

sentences.zh: 高士廉涉獵古今，心術聰悟，臨難既不改節，為官亦無朋黨；

translations.literal: Gao Shilian ranges broadly over past and present; his mind and methods are perceptive and keen; facing hardship he does not alter his integrity, and in office he forms no faction;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shilian ranges broadly over past and present; his mind is perceptive and keen; he does not alter his integrity in hardship and forms no faction in office;

sentences.zh: 所少者骨鯁規諫耳。

translations.literal: What he lacks is blunt, bone-in-the-throat remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: What he lacks is blunt remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 唐儉言辭便利，善和解人，酒杯流行，發言啟齒；

translations.literal: Tang Jian is fluent in speech and skilled at reconciling people; when wine cups circulate, he opens his mouth to speak;
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jian is fluent in speech and skilled at reconciling people; when wine cups circulate, he opens his mouth to speak;

sentences.zh: 事朕三十載，遂無一言論國家得失。

translations.literal: Yet in thirty years of serving me, he has never once spoken of the state's strengths and faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in thirty years of serving me, he has never once spoken of the state's strengths and faults.

sentences.zh: 楊師道性行純善，自無愆過；

translations.literal: Yang Shidao's nature and conduct are pure and good; on his own he has no fault or failing;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shidao's nature and conduct are pure and good; on his own he has no fault;

sentences.zh: 而情實怯懦，未甚任事，緩急不可得力。

translations.literal: Yet in truth he is timid and weak, not very effective in office; in urgent matters one cannot rely on his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in truth he is timid and weak, not very effective in office; in urgent matters one cannot rely on him.

sentences.zh: 岑文本性道惇厚，文章是其所長；

translations.literal: Cen Wende's character and path are sincere and thick; literary composition is his strong point;
translations.idiomatic: Cen Wende's character is sincere and steadfast; literary composition is his strong point;

sentences.zh: 而持論常據經遠，自當不負於物。

translations.literal: Yet his arguments always rest on the classics and reach far; on his own he surely does not fail others.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his arguments always rest on the classics and reach far; on his own he surely does not fail others.

sentences.zh: 劉洎性最堅貞，言多利益；

translations.literal: Liu Ji's nature is the most firm and steadfast; his words are mostly beneficial;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji's nature is the most firm and steadfast; his words are mostly beneficial;

sentences.zh: 然其意上然諾於朋友，能自補闕，亦何以尚。

translations.literal: Yet in intent he is overly ready to assent to friends; that he can himself remedy his shortcomings is still admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he is overly ready to assent to friends; that he can remedy his own shortcomings is still admirable.

sentences.zh: 馬周見事敏速，性甚貞正，至於論量人物，直道而行，朕比任使，多所稱意。

translations.literal: Ma Zhou sees affairs with keen speed; his nature is very upright and correct; as for judging and measuring people, he walks the straight path—when I have recently employed him, I have been well pleased in many respects.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou sees affairs with keen speed; his nature is very upright; in judging people he walks the straight path—when I have recently employed him, I have been well pleased in many respects.

sentences.zh: 褚遂良學問稍長，性亦堅正，既寫忠誠，甚親附於朕，譬如飛鳥依人，自加憐愛。

translations.literal: Chu Suiliang's learning is somewhat advanced and his nature likewise firm and correct; having written out his loyalty, he is very close and attached to me—like a flying bird clinging to a person, I naturally feel added affection for him.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang's learning is somewhat advanced and his nature likewise firm and upright; having shown his loyalty, he is very close to me—like a bird clinging to a person, I naturally feel added affection for him.

sentences.zh: 」十九年，太宗征高麗，令無忌攝侍中。

translations.literal: " In the nineteenth year Taizong campaigned against Goguryeo and ordered Wuji to act as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: " In the nineteenth year Taizong campaigned against Goguryeo and ordered Wuji to serve as acting Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 還，無忌固辭師傅之位，優詔聽罷太子太師。

translations.literal: On his return Wuji firmly declined the position of tutor; a gracious edict permitted him to relinquish the post of Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Wuji firmly declined the post of tutor; a gracious edict permitted him to relinquish the office of Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，遙領揚州都督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he nominally held the post of Governor-General of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was made Governor-General of Yangzhou in absentia.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，太宗疾篤，引無忌及中書令褚遂良二人受遺令輔政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Taizong fell critically ill and summoned Wuji and the Director of the Secretariat Chu Suiliang to receive his deathbed testament and assist in governing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year Taizong fell critically ill and summoned Wuji and Director of the Secretariat Chu Suiliang to receive his deathbed testament and serve as regents.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂遂良曰：「無忌盡忠於我，我有天下，多是此人力。

translations.literal: Taizong said to Suiliang, "Wuji has served me with complete loyalty; that I possess the realm is largely this man's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said to Suiliang, "Wuji has served me with complete loyalty. That I hold the realm is largely owing to him.

sentences.zh: 爾輔政後，勿令讒毀之徒損害無忌。

translations.literal: After you assist in governing, do not let those who slander and malign harm Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: After you take up the regency, do not allow slanderers to do him harm.

sentences.zh: 若如此者，爾則非復人臣。」

translations.literal: If you act thus, you will no longer be a true minister."
translations.idiomatic: If you do otherwise, you will no longer be worthy of the name minister."

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，進拜太尉，兼揚州都督，知尚書及門下二省事並如故。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, Wuji was promoted to Grand Commandant, concurrently Governor-General of Yangzhou, and continued as before to oversee the Secretariat and the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong ascended the throne, Wuji was promoted to Grand Commandant, made concurrent Governor-General of Yangzhou, and continued to oversee the Secretariat and Chancellery as before.

sentences.zh: 無忌固辭知尚書省事，許之，仍令以太尉同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Wuji firmly declined to oversee the Secretariat; this was granted, and he was still ordered to hold the rank of Grand Commandant at the same level as the Three Departments at third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji firmly declined oversight of the Secretariat, and his request was granted; he retained the post of Grand Commandant with third-rank standing equal to the heads of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui he supervised compilation of the dynastic history.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonghui he was put in charge of compiling the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘗謂公卿：「朕開獻書之路，冀有意見可錄，將擢用之。

translations.literal: Gaozong once said to the court officials, "I have opened the way for submitting writings, hoping there would be views worth recording that I might promote and employ.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong once told the court officials, "I opened the way for submitted writings, hoping to find views worth recording and promote those who offered them.

sentences.zh: 比者上疏雖多，而遂無可採者。

translations.literal: Of late, although memorials have been many, there have proved to be none fit to adopt.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately, though memorials pour in, none have proved worth adopting.

sentences.zh: 」無忌對曰：「陛下即位，政化流行，條式律令，固無遺闕。

translations.literal: Wuji replied, "Since Your Majesty took the throne, government and transformation have prevailed; regulations, models, and statutes are indeed without omission or lapse.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji replied, "Since Your Majesty took the throne, governance has flourished, and regulations and statutes leave no gap.

sentences.zh: 言事者率其鄙見，妄希僥倖，至於裨俗益教，理當無足可取。

translations.literal: Those who speak on affairs generally bring forth their shallow views and rashly hope for lucky chance; as for truly benefiting custom and improving instruction, it stands to reason that there is little worth taking.
translations.idiomatic: Those who speak on affairs mostly offer shallow views and grasp at fortune; as for truly benefitting custom and instruction, little is likely worth adopting.

sentences.zh: 然須開此路，猶冀時有讜言，如或杜絕，便恐下情不達。

translations.literal: Yet this path must remain open, still hoping that from time to time there will be forthright speech; if it were cut off, one would fear that sentiments below could not reach the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this channel must stay open, so that forthright counsel may still occasionally reach you; cut it off, and the concerns of those below may never be heard.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「又聞所在官司，猶自多有顏面。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "I also hear that in the offices everywhere there is still much showing of face.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I also hear that officials everywhere still show favoritism based on personal connections.

sentences.zh: 」無忌曰：「顏面阿私，自古不免。

translations.literal: Wuji said, "Showing face and partiality has from antiquity been impossible to eliminate entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji said, "Such partiality based on personal ties has never been wholly absent.

sentences.zh: 然聖化所漸，人皆向公，至於肆情曲法，實謂必無此事。

translations.literal: Yet where sagely transformation has seeped in, all turn toward the public good; as for indulging feelings and bending the law, I truly say this cannot be happening now.
translations.idiomatic: Yet under your sage rule all incline toward the public good; as for wilful bending of the law, I truly believe it no longer occurs.

sentences.zh: 小小收取人情，恐陛下尚亦不免，況臣下私其親戚，豈敢頓言絕無？

translations.literal: In small matters accepting human favor—Your Majesty perhaps could not wholly avoid this either; how much more so when subordinates favor their own kin—how dare I abruptly declare that there is absolutely none?
translations.idiomatic: Even in small matters of accepting favors, Your Majesty may not be wholly exempt; how much more subordinates who favor their kin—I dare not claim there is none at all.

sentences.zh: 」時無忌位當元舅，數進謀議，高宗無不優納之。

translations.literal: At this time Wuji stood as chief maternal uncle; he repeatedly offered counsel, and Gaozong never failed to receive it graciously.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Wuji was the Emperor's chief maternal uncle; he repeatedly offered counsel, and Gaozong always received it with favor.

sentences.zh: 明年，以旱上疏辭職，高宗頻降手詔敦喻不許。

translations.literal: The next year, citing drought, he submitted a memorial resigning office; Gaozong repeatedly sent imperial autographs urging and instructing him, and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he cited drought in a memorial resigning his post; Gaozong repeatedly sent personal edicts urging him to stay and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 五年，親幸無忌第，見其三子，並擢授朝散大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Emperor personally visited Wuji's residence, saw his three sons, and all were promoted and appointed Gentlemen for Spreading Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Emperor personally visited Wuji's home, saw his three sons, and appointed them all Gentlemen for Spreading Virtue.

sentences.zh: 又命圖無忌形像，親為畫贊以賜之。

translations.literal: He also ordered Wuji's likeness painted and personally composed an inscription for the portrait to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered a portrait of Wuji painted and personally wrote an encomium on it as a gift.

sentences.zh: 六年，帝將立昭儀武氏為皇后，無忌屢言不可，帝乃密遣使賜無忌金銀寶器各一車、綾錦十車，以悅其意。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Emperor was about to establish Lady Wu, Lady of Bright Deportment, as empress; Wuji repeatedly said it could not be done, so the Emperor secretly sent envoys to bestow on Wuji one cart each of gold, silver, and precious vessels and ten carts of brocades and silks, to please his mind.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Emperor intended to make Lady Wu, Lady of Bright Deportment, empress; Wuji repeatedly objected, so the Emperor secretly sent envoys laden with carts of gold, silver, precious vessels, and silks to win him over.

sentences.zh: 昭儀母楊氏復自詣無忌宅，屢加祈請。

translations.literal: The Lady of Bright Deportment's mother, Lady Yang, also came in person to Wuji's house and repeatedly pressed him with pleas.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu's mother, Lady Yang, also came in person to Wuji's home and repeatedly entreated him.

sentences.zh: 時禮部尚書許敬宗又屢申勸請，無忌嘗厲色折之。

translations.literal: At the time the Minister of Rites Xu Jingzong also repeatedly pressed his counsel and pleas; Wuji once rebuffed him with a stern countenance.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Minister of Rites Xu Jingzong also pressed him repeatedly; Wuji once rebuffed him with a stern face.

sentences.zh: 帝后又召無忌、左僕射於志寧、右僕射褚遂良，謂曰：「武昭儀有令德，朕欲立為皇后，卿等以為如何？

translations.literal: The Emperor again summoned Wuji, Left Vice Minister Yu Zhining, and Right Vice Minister Chu Suiliang, and said, "Lady Wu, Lady of Bright Deportment, possesses outstanding virtue; I wish to establish her as empress—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again summoned Wuji, Left Vice Minister Yu Zhining, and Right Vice Minister Chu Suiliang and said, "Lady Wu possesses outstanding virtue, and I wish to make her empress. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 」無忌曰：「自貞觀二十三年後，先朝付託遂良，望陛下問其可否。

translations.literal: Wuji said, "Since the twenty-third year of Zhenguan, the late Emperor entrusted Suiliang; I hope Your Majesty will ask him whether it is permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji said, "Since the twenty-third year of Zhenguan the late Emperor entrusted Suiliang. I hope Your Majesty will ask him whether this is permissible.

sentences.zh: 」帝竟不從無忌等言而立昭儀為皇后。

translations.literal: The Emperor ultimately did not follow the words of Wuji and the others and established the Lady of Bright Deportment as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ultimately disregarded Wuji and the others and made Lady of Bright Deportment empress.

sentences.zh: 皇后以無忌先受重賞而不助己，心甚銜之。

translations.literal: The Empress, because Wuji had first received rich rewards yet did not assist her, bore deep resentment in her heart.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress deeply resented Wuji, who had accepted lavish gifts yet refused to support her.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，無忌與史官國子祭酒令狐德棻綴集武德、貞觀二朝史為八十捲，表上之，無忌以監領功，賜物二千段，封其子潤為金城縣子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing, Wuji together with the historian and Chancellor of the Directorate of Education Linghu Defen compiled the histories of the Wude and Zhenguan reigns into eighty juan, submitted them in a memorial, and Wuji for his merit in supervising received two thousand rolls of gifts; his son Run was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jincheng County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianqing, Wuji and the historian Linghu Defen, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, compiled the histories of the Wude and Zhenguan reigns into eighty juan and submitted them. Wuji received two thousand rolls of gifts for supervising the work, and his son Run was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 四年，中書令許敬宗遣人上封事，稱監察御史李巢與無忌交通謀反，帝令敬宗與侍中辛茂將鞠之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Director of the Secretariat Xu Jingzong had someone submit a sealed memorial accusing the Imperial Censor Li Chao of colluding with Wuji in a plot to rebel; the Emperor ordered Jingzong and the Palace Attendant Xin Maojiang to investigate it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Director of the Secretariat Xu Jingzong had a sealed memorial submitted accusing Imperial Censor Li Chao of conspiring with Wuji to rebel. The Emperor ordered Jingzong and Palace Attendant Xin Maojiang to investigate.

sentences.zh: 敬宗奏言無忌謀反有端，帝曰：「我家不幸，親戚中頻有惡事。

translations.literal: Jingzong reported that Wuji's rebellion had established traces; the Emperor said, "My house is unlucky—among my kinsmen wicked deeds occur again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong reported that there was substance to the charge of Wuji's rebellion. The Emperor said, "My house is ill-fated—again and again my kinsmen turn to wickedness.

sentences.zh: 高陽公主與朕同氣，往年遂與房遺愛謀反，今阿舅復作噁心。

translations.literal: Princess Gaoyang shares my blood; in former years she plotted rebellion with Fang Yiai, and now my maternal uncle again harbors a foul heart.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Gaoyang is my own sister—years ago she plotted rebellion with Fang Yiai—and now my maternal uncle again turns to evil.

sentences.zh: 近親如此，使我慚見萬姓。

translations.literal: When close kin are like this, it makes me ashamed to face the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: When even my closest kin behave thus, how can I face the people?

sentences.zh: 」敬宗曰：「房遺愛乳臭兒，與女子謀反，豈得成事？

translations.literal: Jingzong said, "Fang Yiai was a suckling babe; plotting rebellion with a woman—how could he have succeeded?
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong said, "Fang Yiai was a callow youth who plotted rebellion with a woman—how could he have succeeded?

sentences.zh: 且無忌與先朝謀取天下，眾人服其智，作宰相三十年，百姓畏其威，可謂威能服物，智能動眾。

translations.literal: Moreover Wuji joined the late Emperor in scheming to win the realm; the multitude admires his wisdom; he has served as chancellor for thirty years and the common people fear his majesty—one may say his awe can subdue things and his wisdom can move the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: But Wuji helped the late Emperor win the realm; all respect his wisdom. He has been chancellor for thirty years, and the people fear his authority—his power subdues men and his wisdom moves multitudes.

sentences.zh: 臣恐無忌知事露，即為急計，攘袂一呼，嘯命同惡，必為宗廟深憂。

translations.literal: Your subject fears that if Wuji learns the affair is exposed, he will at once resort to desperate measures—roll up his sleeves, shout once, rally the wicked by command—and this would surely bring deep grief to the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that if Wuji learns the plot is exposed, he will act at once—roll up his sleeves, summon his allies—and bring grave calamity upon the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 誠願陛下斷之，不日即收捕，准法破家。

translations.literal: I truly wish Your Majesty would decide the matter; within days seize and arrest him and, according to law, destroy his house.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to act decisively—seize him at once and, by law, ruin his house.

sentences.zh: 」帝泣曰：「我決不忍處分與罪，後代良史道我不能和其親戚，使至於此。

translations.literal: The Emperor wept and said, "I absolutely cannot bear to punish and convict him; future good historians will say that I could not harmonize with my kinsmen, and things came to this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wept and said, "I cannot bear to punish him. Future historians will say I failed to keep peace in my own family and allowed matters to come to this.

sentences.zh: 」敬宗曰：「漢文帝漢室明主，薄昭即是帝舅，從代來日，亦有大勳，與無忌不別。

translations.literal: Jingzong said, "Emperor Wen of Han was an enlightened ruler of the Han house; Bo Zhao was the Emperor's maternal uncle; from the days when the Emperor came from Dai he too had great merit—no different from Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong said, "Emperor Wen of Han was a sage ruler; Bo Zhao was the Emperor's uncle and had great merit from the days at Dai—much like Wuji.

sentences.zh: 於後惟坐殺人，文帝惜國之法，令朝臣喪服就宅，哭而殺之，良史不以為失。

translations.literal: Later he was convicted only of murder; Emperor Wen, cherishing the law of the state, had court ministers don mourning dress and go to his house, weep, and then kill him—and good historians did not deem this a fault.
translations.idiomatic: Later Bo Zhao was convicted only of murder. Emperor Wen, upholding the law of the land, had ministers go to his house in mourning dress, weep for him, and then execute him—and good historians did not judge him harshly.

sentences.zh: 今無忌忘先朝之大德，舍陛下之至親，聽受邪謀，遂懷悖逆，意在塗炭生靈。

translations.literal: Now Wuji has forgotten the great kindness of the late court, abandoned Your Majesty's closest kin, listened to and accepted wicked plotting, and thus harbors rebellion, intending to plunge the living multitude into fire and ashes.
translations.idiomatic: Now Wuji has forgotten the late Emperor's great kindness, abandoned his sovereign kin, and heeded wicked plotting, harboring rebellion and intent to bring calamity upon the people.

sentences.zh: 若比薄昭罪惡，未可同年而語，案諸刑典，合誅五族。

translations.literal: Compared with Bo Zhao's crimes, his sins cannot be spoken of in the same breath; according to the penal codes, he merits execution of five clans.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Bo Zhao, his crimes are far graver; by the penal code, his whole clan deserves death.

sentences.zh: 臣聞當斷不斷，反受其亂，大機之事，間不容髮，若少遲延，恐即生變，惟請早決！

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that he who should decide yet does not will instead suffer disorder; in great critical affairs not a hair's breadth may intervene—if there is the slightest delay, I fear a change will arise at once; I ask only that Your Majesty decide early!
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that hesitation in a moment that demands decision brings chaos; in a matter this critical, not a moment may be lost. Delay, and disaster may follow—I beg you to decide at once!

sentences.zh: 」帝竟不親問無忌謀反所由，惟聽敬宗誣構之說，遂去其官爵，流黔州，仍遣使發次州府兵援送至流所。

translations.literal: The Emperor ultimately did not personally question the source of Wuji's alleged rebellion but listened only to Jingzong's fabricated accusations; he then removed Wuji's rank and office, exiled him to Qian Prefecture, and still sent envoys to mobilize troops from successive prefectures and commanderies to escort him to his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor never questioned Wuji himself but accepted Jingzong's fabrications. He stripped Wuji of rank and office, exiled him to Qian Prefecture, and dispatched troops from successive prefectures to escort him there.

sentences.zh: 其子秘書監、駙馬都尉沖等併除名，流於嶺外。

translations.literal: His sons—the Director of the Palace Library and Commandant of Cavaliers Attendant Chong and the rest—were all struck from the registers and exiled beyond the Ling Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: His sons, including Director of the Palace Library and Commandant of Cavaliers Attendant Chong, were all struck from the registers and exiled beyond the Ling Mountains.

sentences.zh: 敬宗尋與吏部尚書李義府遣大理正袁公瑜就黔州重鞫無忌反狀，公瑜逼令自縊而死，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Jingzong soon together with the Minister of the Civil Office Li Yifu dispatched the chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Gongyu to Qian Prefecture to re-examine Wuji's state of rebellion; Gongyu forced him to hang himself, and his household was registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong and Minister of the Civil Office Li Yifu soon sent chief judge Yuan Gongyu to Qian Prefecture to re-examine the charge of rebellion. Gongyu forced Wuji to hang himself, and his household goods were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 無忌既有大功，而死非其罪，天下至今哀之。

translations.literal: Wuji had great merit, yet died for a crime not his; the realm to this day mourns him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji had earned great merit, yet died for a crime he did not commit. The realm mourns him still.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，優詔追復無忌官爵，特令無忌孫延主齊獻公之祀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan a gracious edict posthumously restored Wuji's rank and office, and specially ordered Wuji's grandson Yan to preside over the sacrifices to Duke of Qi Who Offered Abdication.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shangyuan a gracious edict posthumously restored Wuji's rank and titles and appointed his grandson Yan to maintain the ancestral sacrifices to Duke of Qi Who Offered Abdication.

sentences.zh: 無忌從父兄安世，仕王世充，署為內史令，東都平，死於獄中。

translations.literal: Wuji's older first cousin Anshi served Wang Shichong and was appointed Director of the Secretariat; when the Eastern Capital was pacified he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji's elder first cousin Anshi served Wang Shichong as Director of the Secretariat; when the Eastern Capital fell he died in prison.

sentences.zh: 安世子祥，以文德皇后近屬，累除刑部尚書，坐與無忌通書見殺。

translations.literal: Anshi's son Xiang, as a close kinsman of Empress Wende, was repeatedly appointed Minister of Justice; he was executed for the offense of exchanging letters with Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi's son Xiang, a close kinsman of Empress Wende, rose to Minister of Justice; he was executed for corresponding with Wuji.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：士廉才望素高，操秉無玷，保君臣終始之義，為子孫襲繼之謀。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Shilian's talent and reputation have long been high, his conduct and integrity without stain; he preserved to the end the righteousness between ruler and minister and laid plans for his descendants' continuation.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Shilian's talent and standing were always high, his integrity unstained. He kept faith with his sovereign to the end and planned wisely for his descendants.

sentences.zh: 社稷之臣，功亦隆矣；

translations.literal: A pillar of the state—his merit too was lofty;
translations.idiomatic: A pillar of the state, his achievements were great;

sentences.zh: 獎遇之恩，賞亦厚矣。

translations.literal: the grace of reward and favor—his gifts too were generous.
translations.idiomatic: the honors he received were lavish.

sentences.zh: 及子真行，手刃其子，何凶忍也？

translations.literal: Yet when his son Zhenxing reached this point, he personally bladed his own son—how cruel and ruthless!
translations.idiomatic: Yet when it came to his son Zhenxing, he killed his own child with his own hand—how savage!

sentences.zh: 若是積慶之道，不其惑哉！

translations.literal: If this is the way of accumulated blessing, is it not perplexing indeed!
translations.idiomatic: If this is how virtue is rewarded in a family line, how perplexing!

sentences.zh: 無忌戚裡右族，英冠人傑，定立儲闈，力安社稷，勳庸茂著，終始不渝。

translations.literal: Wuji, of the imperial affinal clan and a great house, towered above other men of outstanding talent; he fixed the Heir Apparent in the Eastern Palace and by force settled the altars of soil and grain; his achievements and service were luxuriantly evident, and from beginning to end he did not waver.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji, of the imperial kin and a great clan, stood above the finest men of his age. He secured the heir, steadied the state, and served with conspicuous merit, never wavering to the end.

sentences.zh: 及黜廢中宮，竟不阿旨，報先帝之顧托，為敬宗之誣構。

translations.literal: When it came to deposing the empress of the inner palace, he ultimately would not flatter the imperial wish; he answered the late Emperor's entrustment, and fell victim to Jingzong's fabricated frame-up.
translations.idiomatic: When the legitimate empress was to be deposed, he refused to assent, honoring the late Emperor's trust—and fell victim to Jingzong's fabricated charges.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 忠信獲罪，今古不免；

translations.literal: The loyal and faithful convicted of crime—from antiquity to the present it cannot be avoided;
translations.idiomatic: The loyal and faithful punished for crime—it has ever been thus;

sentences.zh: 無名受戮，族滅何辜！

translations.literal: receiving execution without established guilt—when the clan is extinguished, what crime did they have!
translations.idiomatic: yet to die without proven guilt, and with an innocent clan destroyed!

sentences.zh: 主暗臣奸，足貽後代。

translations.literal: A dim sovereign and treacherous ministers—enough to bequeath as a warning to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: A dim sovereign and treacherous ministers—a lesson enough for posterity.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：嚴嚴申公，功名始終。

translations.literal: Encomium says: stern and stately Duke Shen—merit and fame from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Stern and steadfast Duke Shen—merit and fame held from first to last.

sentences.zh: 文皇題品，信謂酌中。

translations.literal: The Literary Emperor's inscribed appraisal—truly may be called measured to the middle.
translations.idiomatic: The Literary Emperor's appraisal of him was indeed perfectly balanced.

sentences.zh: 趙公右戚，兩朝宣力。

translations.literal: Duke of Zhao, imperial affinal kin—across two reigns he proclaimed his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Zhao, kin by imperial marriage—he served both reigns with force.

sentences.zh: 功成不去，竟逢鬼域。

translations.literal: Merit achieved yet he did not withdraw—in the end he met the realm of ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: Having achieved merit he did not withdraw—and in the end met destruction in the land of ghosts.
